title.zh: 卷一百四十五 列傳第三十三 姚廣孝 張玉 朱能 丘福 譚淵 王真 陳亨
title.en: Volume 145 Biographies 33: Yao Guangxiao, Zhang Yu, Zhu Neng, Qiu Fu, Tan Yuan, Wang Zhen, Chen Heng
title.raw: 卷一百四十五 列傳第三十三 姚廣孝 張玉 朱能 丘福 譚淵 王真 陳亨 Volume 145 Biographies 33: Yao Guangxiao, Zhang Yu, Zhu Neng, Qiu Fu, Tan Yuan, Wang Zhen, Chen Heng

sentences.zh: 姚廣孝張玉子:輗 軏 從子:信朱能邱福附:李遠 王忠 王聰 火真譚淵王真陳亨子:懋附:徐理 房寬 劉才

translations.literal: Yao Guangxiao, Zhang Yu, sons: Yi, Yue, nephew: Xin, Zhu Neng, Qiu Fu, appended: Li Yuan, Wang Zhong, Wang Cong, Huo Zhen, Tan Yuan, Wang Zhen, Chen Heng, son: Mao, appended: Xu Li, Fang Kuan, Liu Cai.
translations.idiomatic: Biographies of Yao Guangxiao and Zhang Yu (sons Yi and Yue; nephew Xin); Zhu Neng and Qiu Fu; with appended biographies of Li Yuan, Wang Zhong, Wang Cong, and Huo Zhen; Tan Yuan, Wang Zhen, and Chen Heng (son Mao); with appended biographies of Xu Li, Fang Kuan, and Liu Cai.

sentences.zh: 姚廣孝

translations.literal: Yao Guangxiao.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Guangxiao

sentences.zh: 姚廣孝，長洲人，本醫家子。

translations.literal: Yao Guangxiao, a man of Changzhou, was originally the son of a physician's family.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Guangxiao, a native of Changzhou, came from a family of physicians.

sentences.zh: 年十四，度為僧，名道衍，字斯道。

translations.literal: At age fourteen he was tonsured as a monk, named Daoyan, styled Sidao.
translations.idiomatic: At fourteen he took monastic vows under the name Daoyan, with the style Sidao.

sentences.zh: 事道士席應真，得其陰陽術數之學。

translations.literal: He served the Daoist Xi Yingzhen and obtained his learning in yin-yang arts and numerical divination.
translations.idiomatic: He studied under the Daoist Xi Yingzhen and mastered the arts of yin-yang cosmology and divination.

sentences.zh: 嘗遊嵩山寺，相者袁珙見之曰：「是何異僧！

translations.literal: Once he visited Songshan Temple; the physiognomist Yuan Gong saw him and said, "What a strange monk!
translations.idiomatic: Once, while visiting Songshan Temple, the physiognomist Yuan Gong saw him and exclaimed, "What an extraordinary monk!

sentences.zh: 目三角，形如病虎，性必嗜殺，劉秉忠流也。

translations.literal: Triangular eyes, form like a sick tiger—his nature must love killing; he is of the stream of Liu Bingzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Triangular eyes, the bearing of a sick tiger—he is bound to be bloodthirsty by nature, a man in the line of Liu Bingzhong."

sentences.zh: 」道衍大喜。

translations.literal: " Daoyan was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Daoyan was delighted.

sentences.zh: 洪武中，詔通儒書僧試禮部。

translations.literal: In the Hongwu period, an edict summoned monks versed in Confucian books to be examined at the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: During the Hongwu reign, an edict called for monks trained in the Confucian classics to sit for examinations at the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 不受官，賜僧服還。

translations.literal: He did not accept office; he was given monastic robes and sent back.
translations.idiomatic: He declined official appointment and was given monastic robes and sent home.

sentences.zh: 經北固山，賦詩懷古。

translations.literal: Passing Beigu Mountain, he composed a poem contemplating antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Passing Beigu Mountain, he composed a poem meditating on the past.

sentences.zh: 其儕宗泐曰：「此豈釋子語耶？

translations.literal: His fellow monk Zong Le said, "How can this be the speech of a Buddhist disciple?
translations.idiomatic: His fellow monk Zong Le said, "Is this really the language of a Buddhist monk?

sentences.zh: 」道衍笑不答。

translations.literal: " Daoyan smiled and did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Daoyan only smiled and said nothing.

sentences.zh: 高皇后崩，太祖選高僧侍諸王，為誦經薦福。

translations.literal: When Empress Gao died, the Founding Emperor selected eminent monks to attend the princes and chant sutras to recommend blessings.
translations.idiomatic: After the death of Empress Gao, the Hongwu Emperor chose eminent monks to attend the princes and recite sutras for the dead.

sentences.zh: 宗泐時為左善世，舉道衍。

translations.literal: Zong Le was then Left Director of the Buddhist Registry and recommended Daoyan.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Le, who was then Director of the Left Buddhist Registry, recommended Daoyan.

sentences.zh: 燕王與語甚合，請以從。

translations.literal: The Prince of Yan conversed with him and found great agreement, and asked that he accompany him.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Yan found him congenial in conversation and asked that he accompany him.

sentences.zh: 至北平，住持慶壽寺。

translations.literal: Arriving at Beiping, he became abbot of Qingshou Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Upon reaching Beiping, he became abbot of Qingshou Temple.

sentences.zh: 出入府中，跡甚密，時時屏人語。

translations.literal: He went in and out of the princely residence; his tracks were very close, and from time to time he dismissed attendants to speak.
translations.idiomatic: He came and went within the princely mansion with great frequency, often dismissing others so they could speak in private.

sentences.zh: 及太祖崩，惠帝立，以次削奪諸王。

translations.literal: When the Founding Emperor died and Emperor Hui ascended, in sequence the princes were stripped and dispossessed.
translations.idiomatic: After the Hongwu Emperor's death, when Emperor Hui came to the throne, the court began systematically weakening the princes.

sentences.zh: 周、湘、代、齊、岷相繼得罪。

translations.literal: The princes of Zhou, Xiang, Dai, Qi, and Min successively met with punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The princes of Zhou, Xiang, Dai, Qi, and Min were ruined one after another.

sentences.zh: 道衍遂密勸成祖舉兵。

translations.literal: Daoyan then secretly urged Chengzu to raise troops.
translations.idiomatic: Daoyan then secretly urged the Prince of Yan to take up arms.

sentences.zh: 成祖曰：「民心向彼，奈何？

translations.literal: Chengzu said, "The people's hearts turn toward him—what is to be done?
translations.idiomatic: The prince said, "The people favor him—what can we do?

sentences.zh: 」道衍曰：「臣知天道，何論民心。

translations.literal: " Daoyan said, "Your servant knows Heaven's Way—why discuss the people's hearts?
translations.idiomatic: Daoyan replied, "I know Heaven's mandate—why speak of popular sentiment?

sentences.zh: 」乃進袁珙及卜者金忠。

translations.literal: " He then presented Yuan Gong and the diviner Jin Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: He then introduced Yuan Gong and the diviner Jin Zhong.

sentences.zh: 於是成祖意益決。

translations.literal: Thereupon Chengzu's mind grew ever more resolved.
translations.idiomatic: The prince's resolve hardened still further.

sentences.zh: 陰選將校，勾軍卒，收材勇異能之士。

translations.literal: In secret he selected commanders, enlisted soldiers, and gathered men of talent, courage, and special ability.
translations.idiomatic: In secret he chose officers, recruited soldiers, and gathered men of talent, courage, and exceptional skill.

sentences.zh: 燕邸，故元宮也，深邃。

translations.literal: The Yan residence was the former Yuan palace, deep and secluded.
translations.idiomatic: The Yan princely residence was a former Yuan palace, vast and secluded.

sentences.zh: 道衍練兵後苑中。

translations.literal: Daoyan drilled troops in the rear garden.
translations.idiomatic: Daoyan trained troops in the rear garden.

sentences.zh: 穴地作重屋，繚以厚垣，密甃翎甋瓶缶，日夜鑄軍器，畜鵝鴨亂其聲。

translations.literal: They dug the ground to make a multi-storied structure, surrounded it with thick walls, densely paved with tiles and jars and pots, day and night casting weapons, keeping geese and ducks to confuse the sound.
translations.idiomatic: They excavated underground chambers walled with thick ramparts, lined them with tiles and jars, cast weapons day and night, and kept geese and ducks to mask the noise.

sentences.zh: 建文元年六月，燕府護衛百戶倪諒上變。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the first year of Jianwen, Ni Liang, a hundred-household officer of the Yan residence guard, reported a treasonous plot.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the first year of the Jianwen reign, Ni Liang, a hundred-household officer of the Yan princely guard, denounced the prince for treason.

sentences.zh: 詔逮府中官屬。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the arrest of officials in the residence.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the arrest of the prince's household officials.

sentences.zh: 都指揮張信輸誠於成祖，成祖遂決策起兵。

translations.literal: The commander-in-chief Zhang Xin pledged loyalty to Chengzu, and Chengzu then decided to raise troops.
translations.idiomatic: The regional commander Zhang Xin declared his loyalty to the prince, who then resolved to rise in arms.

sentences.zh: 適大風雨至，檐瓦墮地，成祖色變。

translations.literal: Just then a great wind and rain came; eaves-tiles fell to the ground, and Chengzu's countenance changed.
translations.idiomatic: Just then a violent storm struck; roof tiles crashed to the ground, and the prince's face fell.

sentences.zh: 道衍曰：「祥也。

translations.literal: Daoyan said, "This is auspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Daoyan said, "This is a good omen.

sentences.zh: 飛龍在天，從以風雨。

translations.literal: The flying dragon is in heaven, followed by wind and rain.
translations.idiomatic: When the flying dragon is in heaven, wind and rain follow.

sentences.zh: 瓦墮，將易黃也。

translations.literal: Tiles fall—the yellow will soon replace them.
translations.idiomatic: Tiles fall because they will soon be replaced by yellow ones."

sentences.zh: 」兵起，以誅齊泰、黃子澄為名，號其眾曰「靖難之師。

translations.literal: " When the army rose, taking as its pretext the punishment of Qi Tai and Huang Zicheng, it named its forces the "Army to Pacify Difficulties."
translations.idiomatic: When the army marched, it took as its cause the punishment of Qi Tai and Huang Zicheng and called its forces the Army to Pacify Difficulties.

sentences.zh: 」道衍輔世子居守。

translations.literal: " Daoyan assisted the heir apparent in holding the residence.
translations.idiomatic: Daoyan remained to assist the heir apparent in defending Beiping.

sentences.zh: 其年十月，成祖襲大寧，李景隆乘間圍北平。

translations.literal: That year in the tenth month, Chengzu raided Daning; Li Jinglong seized the interval to besiege Beiping.
translations.idiomatic: That October the prince struck at Daning, and Li Jinglong took the opportunity to besiege Beiping.

sentences.zh: 道衍守禦甚固，擊卻攻者。

translations.literal: Daoyan defended very firmly and beat back the attackers.
translations.idiomatic: Daoyan mounted a stout defense and drove back the assailants.

sentences.zh: 夜縋壯士擊傷南兵。

translations.literal: By night he lowered brave men by rope to strike and wound the southern troops.
translations.idiomatic: At night he lowered brave men by rope to raid and wound the southern army.

sentences.zh: 援師至，內外合擊，斬首無算。

translations.literal: Relief troops arrived; inside and outside joined in attack, and heads cut off were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: When relief arrived, the defenders sallied forth in concert and slew the enemy beyond count.

sentences.zh: 景隆、平安等先後敗遁。

translations.literal: Jinglong, Ping'an, and others in succession were defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jinglong, Ping'an, and others were defeated in turn and fled.

sentences.zh: 成祖圍濟南三月，不克。

translations.literal: Chengzu besieged Jinan for three months without taking it.
translations.idiomatic: The prince besieged Jinan for three months without success.

sentences.zh: 道衍馳書曰：「師老矣，請班師。

translations.literal: Daoyan sent a hurried letter saying, "The army is weary—please withdraw the forces.
translations.idiomatic: Daoyan sent an urgent message: "The army is exhausted—withdraw it.

sentences.zh: 」乃還。

translations.literal: " He then returned.
translations.idiomatic: The prince then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 復攻東昌，戰敗，亡大將張玉，復還。

translations.literal: He again attacked Dongchang, was defeated in battle, lost the great general Zhang Yu, and returned once more.
translations.idiomatic: He attacked Dongchang again, was defeated, lost the great general Zhang Yu, and withdrew once more.

sentences.zh: 成祖意欲稍休，道衍力趣之。

translations.literal: Chengzu wished to rest somewhat; Daoyan strongly urged him on.
translations.idiomatic: The prince wished to pause, but Daoyan pressed him relentlessly to continue.

sentences.zh: 益募勇士，敗盛庸，破房昭西水寨。

translations.literal: He further recruited brave warriors, defeated Sheng Yong, and broke Fang Zhao's western water camp.
translations.idiomatic: He recruited more brave men, defeated Sheng Yong, and destroyed Fang Zhao's western river encampment.

sentences.zh: 道衍語成祖：「毋下城邑，疾趨京師。

translations.literal: Daoyan told Chengzu, "Do not reduce walled cities—hasten straight to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Daoyan told the prince, "Do not waste time on walled towns—march swiftly on the capital.

sentences.zh: 京師單弱，勢必舉。

translations.literal: The capital is thin and weak; the situation must surely succeed.
translations.idiomatic: The capital is weakly defended and is sure to fall.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " He followed this advice.
translations.idiomatic: The prince followed his counsel.

sentences.zh: 遂連敗諸將於淝河、靈璧，渡江入京師。

translations.literal: He then in succession defeated the generals at the Fei River and Lingbi, crossed the Yangzi, and entered the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He then routed the enemy generals at the Fei River and Lingbi, crossed the Yangzi, and entered the capital.

sentences.zh: 成祖即帝位，授道衍僧錄司左善世。

translations.literal: When Chengzu assumed the imperial throne, he appointed Daoyan Left Director of the Buddhist Registry.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince became emperor, he appointed Daoyan Director of the Left Buddhist Registry.

sentences.zh: 帝在藩邸，所接皆武人，獨道衍定策起兵。

translations.literal: When the Emperor was in his princely residence, those he received were all military men; only Daoyan settled the plan to raise troops.
translations.idiomatic: While still a prince, the emperor's companions had been soldiers; only Daoyan had shaped the plan to rebel.

sentences.zh: 及帝轉戰山東、河北，在軍三年，或旋或否，戰守機事皆決於道衍。

translations.literal: When the Emperor campaigned through Shandong and Hebei, he was in the army three years, sometimes returning and sometimes not; matters of battle, defense, and opportunity were all decided by Daoyan.
translations.idiomatic: During three years of campaigning through Shandong and Hebei, whether the emperor advanced or held back, every strategic decision rested with Daoyan.

sentences.zh: 道衍未嘗臨戰陣，然帝用兵有天下，道衍力為多，論功以為第一。

translations.literal: Daoyan never once faced a battle line, yet the Emperor's use of troops won the realm—Daoyan's strength contributed much, and in reckoning merit he was ranked first.
translations.idiomatic: Daoyan never took the field himself, yet in winning the empire the emperor owed him more than to any other; in the reckoning of merit he ranked first.

sentences.zh: 永樂二年四月，拜資善大夫、太子少師。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the second year of Yongle, he was appointed Grand Master of the Palace Library and Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the second year of Yongle, he was made Grand Master of the Palace Library and Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 復其姓，賜名廣孝，贈祖父如其官。

translations.literal: His surname was restored; he was granted the name Guangxiao, and his grandfather was enfeoffed with titles matching his rank.
translations.idiomatic: His family name was restored, he was granted the name Guangxiao, and his grandfather received posthumous honors matching his rank.

sentences.zh: 帝與語，呼少師而不名。

translations.literal: When the Emperor spoke with him, he called him Junior Tutor without using his name.
translations.idiomatic: In conversation the emperor addressed him as Junior Tutor rather than by name.

sentences.zh: 命蓄髮，不肯。

translations.literal: He was ordered to grow his hair; he refused.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to let his hair grow, but he refused.

sentences.zh: 賜第及兩宮人，皆不受。

translations.literal: A residence and two palace women were bestowed; he accepted none of them.
translations.idiomatic: He declined the mansion and the two palace women the emperor offered him.

sentences.zh: 常居僧寺，冠帶而朝，退仍緇衣。

translations.literal: He constantly dwelt in a Buddhist temple, attended court in cap and sash, and on retiring still wore monastic robes.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in a monastery, wore official dress at court, and returned to his monastic robes afterward.

sentences.zh: 出振蘇、湖，至長洲，以所賜金帛散宗族鄉人。

translations.literal: Going out to bring relief to Suzhou and Huzhou, he reached Changzhou and distributed the gold and silks given him among kinsmen and villagers.
translations.idiomatic: On a relief mission to Suzhou and Huzhou he reached Changzhou and distributed his gifts of gold and silk among his clansmen and neighbors.

sentences.zh: 重修《太祖實錄》，廣孝為監修。

translations.literal: The Veritable Records of the Founding Emperor were revised; Guangxiao served as supervising compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He supervised the revision of the Veritable Records of the Hongwu Emperor.

sentences.zh: 又與解縉等纂修《永樂大典》。

translations.literal: He also joined Xie Jin and others in compiling the Yongle Encyclopedia.
translations.idiomatic: He also joined Xie Jin and others in compiling the Yongle Encyclopedia.

sentences.zh: 書成，帝褒美之。

translations.literal: When the book was completed, the Emperor praised it highly.
translations.idiomatic: When the work was finished, the emperor praised it warmly.

sentences.zh: 帝往來兩都、出塞北征，廣孝皆留輔太子於南京。

translations.literal: When the Emperor traveled between the two capitals or campaigned north beyond the passes, Guangxiao always remained to assist the heir apparent at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor traveled between capitals or campaigned beyond the frontier, Guangxiao stayed in Nanjing to assist the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 五年四月，皇長孫出閣就學，廣孝侍說書。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fifth year, the emperor's eldest grandson left the inner quarters to begin study; Guangxiao attended as lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the fifth year, when the emperor's eldest grandson began formal schooling, Guangxiao served as his tutor.

sentences.zh: 十六年三月，入覲，年八十有四矣，病甚，不能朝，仍居慶壽寺。

translations.literal: In the third month of the sixteenth year he came to audience; he was eighty-four, gravely ill, unable to attend court, and still dwelt at Qingshou Temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the sixteenth year he came to court; he was eighty-four, gravely ill, unable to attend audience, and still lived at Qingshou Temple.

sentences.zh: 車駕臨視者再，語甚歡，賜以金唾壺。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage visited him twice; their talk was very pleasant, and he was given a golden spittoon.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor visited him twice; their conversation was warm, and he was given a golden spittoon.

sentences.zh: 問所欲言，廣孝曰：「僧溥洽繫久，願赦之。

translations.literal: Asked what he wished to say, Guangxiao said, "The monk Pu Qia has been imprisoned long—I beg that he be pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Asked if he had any request, Guangxiao said, "The monk Pu Qia has been imprisoned for many years—I beg that he be pardoned.

sentences.zh: 」溥洽者，建文帝主錄僧也。

translations.literal: " Pu Qia was the chief recording monk of Emperor Jianwen.
translations.idiomatic: Pu Qia had been the chief recording monk under Emperor Jianwen.

sentences.zh: 初，帝入南京，有言建文帝為僧遁去，溥洽知狀，或言匿溥洽所。

translations.literal: At first, when the Emperor entered Nanjing, there was talk that Emperor Jianwen had fled disguised as a monk and that Pu Qia knew the circumstances; some said he was hidden at Pu Qia's place.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor first entered Nanjing, rumor held that Emperor Jianwen had escaped disguised as a monk and that Pu Qia knew his whereabouts; some said the former emperor was hidden with Pu Qia.

sentences.zh: 帝乃以他事禁溥洽。

translations.literal: The Emperor then imprisoned Pu Qia on another charge.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor therefore imprisoned Pu Qia on another pretext.

sentences.zh: 而命給事中胡濙等遍物色建文帝，久之不可得。

translations.literal: He also ordered the supervising secretary Hu Ying and others to search everywhere for Emperor Jianwen; after a long time they could not obtain him.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered the supervising secretary Hu Ying and others to search the realm for Emperor Jianwen, but after a long search they found nothing.

sentences.zh: 溥洽坐繫十餘年。

translations.literal: Pu Qia sat in imprisonment for more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: Pu Qia remained in prison for more than ten years.

sentences.zh: 至是，帝以廣孝言，即命出之。

translations.literal: At this time, because of Guangxiao's words, the Emperor immediately ordered his release.
translations.idiomatic: Now, at Guangxiao's request, the emperor ordered him released at once.

sentences.zh: 廣孝頓首謝。

translations.literal: Guangxiao bowed his head in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Guangxiao kowtowed in gratitude.

sentences.zh: 尋卒。

translations.literal: Soon after he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon afterward.

sentences.zh: 帝震悼，輟視朝二日，命有司治喪，以僧禮葬。

translations.literal: The Emperor was shaken and grieved; he suspended court audiences for two days, ordered the relevant offices to manage the funeral, and buried him with Buddhist rites.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deeply grieved, suspended court for two days, ordered officials to arrange the funeral, and buried him with Buddhist rites.

sentences.zh: 追贈推誠輔國協謀宣力文臣、特進榮祿大夫、上柱國、榮國公，謚恭靖。

translations.literal: Posthumously enfeoffed as the civil minister who with sincere support assists the state, coordinates counsel, and proclaims merit; specially advanced Grand Master of Splendid Happiness; Upper Pillar of the State; Duke of Rong; posthumous title Gongjing.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Rong with the titles of specially advanced Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Upper Pillar of the State, and given the posthumous name Gongjing.

sentences.zh: 賜葬房山縣東北。

translations.literal: Burial was granted in the northeast of Fangshan County.
translations.idiomatic: He was buried in the northeast of Fangshan County by imperial grant.

sentences.zh: 帝親製神道碑誌其功。

translations.literal: The Emperor personally composed a spirit-way stele recording his merits.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor personally composed a spirit-way stele commemorating his achievements.

sentences.zh: 官其養子繼尚寶少卿。

translations.literal: His adopted son Ji was given office as Vice Director of the Imperial Seals.
translations.idiomatic: His adopted son Ji was appointed Vice Director of the Imperial Seals.

sentences.zh: 廣孝少好學，工詩。

translations.literal: Guangxiao from youth loved learning and was skilled in poetry.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Guangxiao loved learning and was accomplished in poetry.

sentences.zh: 與王賓、高啟、楊孟載友善。

translations.literal: He was friendly with Wang Bin, Gao Qi, and Yang Mengzai.
translations.idiomatic: He was on friendly terms with Wang Bin, Gao Qi, and Yang Mengzai.

sentences.zh: 宋濂、蘇伯衡亦推獎之。

translations.literal: Song Lian and Su Boheng also praised and commended him.
translations.idiomatic: Song Lian and Su Boheng also praised him highly.

sentences.zh: 晚著《道餘錄》，頗毀先儒，識者鄙焉。

translations.literal: In his later years he wrote the Record of the Remainder of the Way, which rather slandered the earlier Confucians; those with discernment despised it.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he wrote the Record of the Remainder of the Way, which disparaged the early Confucians; thoughtful readers held it in contempt.

sentences.zh: 其至長洲，候同產姊，姊不納。

translations.literal: When he reached Changzhou, he waited upon his sister by the same mother; she would not receive him.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned to Changzhou, he called on his elder sister, but she refused to see him.

sentences.zh: 訪其友王賓，賓亦不見，但遙語曰：「和尚誤矣，和尚誤矣。

translations.literal: He visited his friend Wang Bin; Bin also would not see him but only called from afar, "The monk is mistaken, the monk is mistaken.
translations.idiomatic: He visited his friend Wang Bin, who likewise refused to receive him and only called out from a distance, "You were wrong, monk—you were wrong.

sentences.zh: 」復往見姊，姊詈之。

translations.literal: " He again went to see his sister; she reviled him.
translations.idiomatic: He went to his sister again, and she cursed him.

sentences.zh: 廣孝惘然。

translations.literal: Guangxiao was lost and dismayed.
translations.idiomatic: Guangxiao was left desolate.

sentences.zh: 洪熙元年，加贈少師，配享成祖廟庭。

translations.literal: In the first year of Hongxi, he was further enfeoffed as Junior Tutor and granted joint sacrifice in Chengzu's temple court.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Hongxi he was further honored as Junior Tutor and granted a place in the sacrifices at the Yongle Emperor's temple.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖九年，世宗諭閣臣曰：「姚廣孝佐命嗣興，勞烈俱有。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Jiajing, Shizong instructed the Grand Secretaries, "Yao Guangxiao assisted the mandate and continued the rise; labor and merit both exist.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Jiajing, the Jiajing Emperor told the Grand Secretaries, "Yao Guangxiao aided the founding of the dynasty and shared in its labors and glory.

sentences.zh: 顧係釋氏之徒，班諸功臣，侑食太廟，恐不足尊敬祖宗。

translations.literal: Yet he was of the Buddhist school; to rank him among the merit ministers and grant him joint sacrifice in the Grand Temple would, I fear, be insufficient to honor the ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was a Buddhist monk; to rank him among the meritorious ministers and grant him a place at the Grand Ancestral Temple may not sufficiently honor our forebears.

sentences.zh: 」於是尚書李時偕大學士張璁、桂萼等議請移祀大興隆寺，太常春秋致祭。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the Minister Li Shi together with Grand Secretaries Zhang Cong, Gui E, and others deliberated and requested that his sacrifice be moved to Daxinglong Temple, with the Court of Imperial Sacrifices offering seasonal rites in spring and autumn.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Rites Li Shi and Grand Secretaries Zhang Cong, Gui E, and others then recommended moving his cult to Daxinglong Temple, with seasonal sacrifices in spring and autumn.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「可」。

translations.literal: An edict said, "Approved."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor assented.

sentences.zh: 張玉，字世美，祥符人。

translations.literal: Zhang Yu, styled Shimei, was a man of Xiangfu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yu, styled Shimei, was a native of Xiangfu.

sentences.zh: 仕元為樞密知院。

translations.literal: He served the Yuan as Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Yuan he served as Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 元亡，從走漠北。

translations.literal: When the Yuan perished, he followed them in flight to the northern desert.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yuan fell, he fled with them into the northern steppe.

sentences.zh: 洪武十八年來歸。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Hongwu he came over in submission.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year of Hongwu he defected to the Ming.

sentences.zh: 從大軍出塞，至捕魚兒海，以功授濟南衛副千戶，遷安慶衛指揮僉事。

translations.literal: He followed the great army beyond the passes to Buyur Lake; for merit he was appointed vice thousand-household of Jinan Guard, then transferred as assistant commander of Anqing Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned beyond the frontier to Buyur Lake and, for his service, was made vice thousand-household of Jinan Guard, then assistant commander of Anqing Guard.

sentences.zh: 又從征遠順、散毛諸洞。

translations.literal: He again followed campaigns against Yuanshun, Sanmao, and other cave districts.
translations.idiomatic: He also campaigned against the Yuanshun and Sanmao cave peoples and other tribes.

sentences.zh: 北逐元人之擾邊者，至鴉寒山還，調燕山左護衛。

translations.literal: Driving north after Yuan raiders who disturbed the border, he returned as far as Yahan Mountain and was transferred to the Yan Mountain Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuing Yuan border raiders north to Yahan Mountain, he returned and was assigned to the Yan Mountain Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 從燕王出塞，至黑松林。

translations.literal: He followed the Prince of Yan beyond the passes to Black Pine Forest.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the Prince of Yan beyond the frontier as far as Black Pine Forest.

sentences.zh: 又從征野人諸部。

translations.literal: He again followed campaigns against the wild-man tribes.
translations.idiomatic: He also campaigned against the forest tribes.

sentences.zh: 以驍果善謀畫為王所親任。

translations.literal: For his valor, resolution, and skill in planning he was personally trusted by the prince.
translations.idiomatic: His courage and strategic talent won the prince's personal trust.

sentences.zh: 建文元年，成祖起兵。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianwen, Chengzu raised troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jianwen the prince rose in arms.

sentences.zh: 玉帥眾奪北平九門，撫諭城內外，三日而定。

translations.literal: Yu led the host to seize Beiping's nine gates, reassured those inside and outside the city, and in three days all was settled.
translations.idiomatic: Yu led the troops in seizing Beiping's nine gates, pacified the city inside and out, and secured it within three days.

sentences.zh: 師將南，玉獻計，遣朱能東攻薊州，殺馬宣，降遵化。

translations.literal: As the army was about to march south, Yu offered a plan: send Zhu Neng east to attack Jizhou, kill Ma Xuan, and reduce Zunhua.
translations.idiomatic: As the army prepared to march south, Yu proposed sending Zhu Neng east to take Jizhou, kill Ma Xuan, and secure Zunhua.

sentences.zh: 分兵下永平、密雲，皆致其精甲以益師。

translations.literal: Dividing forces to reduce Yongping and Miyun, he brought in their fine armor to strengthen the army.
translations.idiomatic: Detaching troops to take Yongping and Miyun, he sent their best armor to reinforce the main force.

sentences.zh: 擢都指揮僉事。

translations.literal: He was promoted to assistant regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to assistant regional commander.

sentences.zh: 是時朝廷遣大兵討燕：都督徐凱軍河間；

translations.literal: At this time the court dispatched great armies against Yan: Regional Commander Xu Kai encamped at Hejian;
translations.idiomatic: The court now sent large armies against the prince: Regional Commander Xu Kai at Hejian;

sentences.zh: 潘忠、楊松軍鄚州；

translations.literal: Pan Zhong and Yang Song encamped at Mozhou;
translations.idiomatic: Pan Zhong and Yang Song encamped at Mozhou;

sentences.zh: 長興侯耿炳文以三十萬眾軍真定。

translations.literal: the Marquis of Changxing, Geng Bingwen, with three hundred thousand men encamped at Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: and the Marquis of Changxing, Geng Bingwen, with three hundred thousand men at Zhending.

sentences.zh: 玉進說曰：「潘、楊勇而無謀，可襲而俘也。

translations.literal: Yu advanced counsel, saying, "Pan and Yang are brave but without strategy—they can be raided and captured.
translations.idiomatic: Yu urged, "Pan and Yang are bold but lack strategy—we can surprise them and take them alive.

sentences.zh: 」成祖命玉將親兵為前鋒，抵樓桑。

translations.literal: " Chengzu ordered Yu to lead the personal guard as vanguard and reach Lousang.
translations.idiomatic: The prince ordered Yu to lead the personal guard as vanguard to Lousang.

sentences.zh: 值中秋，南軍方宴會。

translations.literal: It was Mid-Autumn Festival, and the southern army was feasting.
translations.idiomatic: It was Mid-Autumn Festival, and the southern army was holding a feast.

sentences.zh: 夜半，疾馳破雄縣。

translations.literal: At midnight he galloped swiftly and broke Xiong County.
translations.idiomatic: At midnight he charged and stormed Xiong County.

sentences.zh: 忠、松來援，邀擊於月漾橋，生擒之。

translations.literal: Zhong and Song came to relieve; he intercepted them at Yueyang Bridge and took them alive.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhong and Song came to relieve the city, he ambushed them at Yueyang Bridge and captured them alive.

sentences.zh: 遂克鄚州。

translations.literal: He then took Mozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He then captured Mozhou.

sentences.zh: 自以輕騎覘炳文軍。

translations.literal: He himself went with light cavalry to reconnoiter Bingwen's army.
translations.idiomatic: He personally rode out with light cavalry to scout Geng Bingwen's army.

sentences.zh: 還言：「軍無紀律，其上有敗氣，宜急擊。

translations.literal: Returning he said, "The army lacks discipline; above them there is the air of defeat—they should be struck quickly.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he reported, "Their ranks are undisciplined and defeat hangs over them—we should attack at once.

sentences.zh: 」成祖遂引兵西，至無極，顧諸將謀所向。

translations.literal: " Chengzu then led the army west to Wuji and turned to the generals to deliberate where to go.
translations.idiomatic: The prince then marched west to Wuji and asked his generals which way to turn.

sentences.zh: 諸將以南軍盛，請屯新樂。

translations.literal: The generals, because the southern army was strong, asked to encamp at Xinle.
translations.idiomatic: The generals, seeing the southern army's strength, urged encamping at Xinle.

sentences.zh: 玉曰：「彼雖眾，皆新集。

translations.literal: Yu said, "Though they are numerous, they are all newly gathered.
translations.idiomatic: Yu said, "They are many, but they are newly assembled.

sentences.zh: 我軍乘勝徑趨真定，破之必矣。

translations.literal: Our army, riding victory straight to Zhending, will surely break them.
translations.idiomatic: If we press our advantage straight to Zhending, we are sure to crush them.

sentences.zh: 」成祖喜曰：「吾倚玉足濟大事！

translations.literal: " Chengzu rejoiced and said, "I rely on Yu's feet to accomplish the great affair!
translations.idiomatic: The prince exclaimed, "With Yu at my side I can achieve the great enterprise!

sentences.zh: 」明日抵真定，大破炳文軍，獲副將李堅、寧忠，都督顧成等，斬首三萬。

translations.literal: " The next day they reached Zhending, routed Bingwen's army, captured deputy generals Li Jian and Ning Zhong, Regional Commander Gu Cheng, and others, and cut off thirty thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: The next day they reached Zhending, routed Geng Bingwen's army, captured the deputy generals Li Jian and Ning Zhong and Regional Commander Gu Cheng among others, and slew thirty thousand men.

sentences.zh: 復敗安陸侯吳傑軍。

translations.literal: He again defeated the army of the Marquis of Anlu, Wu Jie.
translations.idiomatic: He also defeated the army of the Marquis of Anlu, Wu Jie.

sentences.zh: 燕兵由是大振。

translations.literal: The Yan troops thereby gained great momentum.
translations.idiomatic: The Yan army's fortunes rose sharply.

sentences.zh: 江陰侯吳高以遼東兵圍永平。

translations.literal: The Marquis of Jiangyin, Wu Gao, with Liaodong troops besieged Yongping.
translations.idiomatic: The Marquis of Jiangyin, Wu Gao, besieged Yongping with Liaodong troops.

sentences.zh: 曹國公李景隆引數十萬眾將攻北平。

translations.literal: the Duke of Cao, Li Jinglong, led several hundred thousand men intending to attack Beiping.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Cao, Li Jinglong, marched on Beiping with several hundred thousand men.

sentences.zh: 成祖與玉謀，先援永平。

translations.literal: Chengzu and Yu plotted to relieve Yongping first.
translations.idiomatic: The prince and Yu agreed to relieve Yongping first.

sentences.zh: 至則高遁走，玉追斬甚眾。

translations.literal: When they arrived, Gao fled; Yu pursued and cut down very many.
translations.idiomatic: When they arrived, Wu Gao fled; Yu pursued and killed many.

sentences.zh: 遂從間道襲大寧，拔其眾而還，次會州。

translations.literal: He then took a hidden route to raid Daning, drew off its forces and returned, and encamped at Huizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He then struck Daning by a hidden route, brought its troops over, and encamped at Huizhou on the return march.

sentences.zh: 初立五軍，以玉將中軍。

translations.literal: When the Five Armies were first established, Yu was made to command the central army.
translations.idiomatic: When the Five Armies were first organized, Yu was placed in command of the central army.

sentences.zh: 時李景隆已圍北平，成祖旋師，大戰於鄭村壩，景隆敗。

translations.literal: At this time Li Jinglong had already besieged Beiping; Chengzu wheeled his army about and fought a great battle at Zhengcun Dam; Jinglong was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jinglong had already besieged Beiping; the prince turned back, fought a great battle at Zhengcun Dam, and routed him.

sentences.zh: 成祖乘勝抵城下。

translations.literal: Chengzu, riding victory, reached below the walls.
translations.idiomatic: Pressing the victory, the prince reached the city walls.

sentences.zh: 城中兵鼓噪出，內外夾攻，南軍大潰。

translations.literal: Troops in the city beat drums and shouted as they sallied forth; inside and outside joined in attack, and the southern army collapsed in great disorder.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison sallied forth with a great clamor; attacked from within and without, the southern army broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 明年從攻廣昌、蔚州、大同。

translations.literal: The next year he followed in attacks on Guangchang, Yuzhou, and Datong.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he campaigned at Guangchang, Yuzhou, and Datong.

sentences.zh: 諜報景隆收潰卒，號百萬，且復至。

translations.literal: Spies reported that Jinglong had gathered routed soldiers, called them a million, and would come again.
translations.idiomatic: Intelligence reported that Li Jinglong had rallied his broken troops, claimed a million men, and was marching again.

sentences.zh: 玉曰：「兵貴神速，請先據白溝河，以逸待勞。

translations.literal: Yu said, "In war speed is precious—please first seize the White Ditch River and await the weary with rested troops.
translations.idiomatic: Yu said, "Speed is everything in war—seize the White Ditch River first and meet their fatigue with fresh troops.

sentences.zh: 」駐河上三日，景隆至。

translations.literal: " They encamped on the river three days; Jinglong arrived.
translations.idiomatic: They held the river for three days until Li Jinglong arrived.

sentences.zh: 以精騎馳擊，復大敗之。

translations.literal: With elite cavalry he galloped to strike and again routed them greatly.
translations.idiomatic: He charged with elite cavalry and routed them again.

sentences.zh: 進拔德州，追奔至濟南，圍其城三月，解圍還。

translations.literal: Advancing he took Dezhou, pursued the fugitives to Jinan, besieged the city three months, lifted the siege, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced to take Dezhou, pursued the enemy to Jinan, besieged the city for three months, then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 尋再出，破滄州，擒徐凱。

translations.literal: Soon he marched out again, broke Cangzhou, and captured Xu Kai.
translations.idiomatic: He marched out again soon after, took Cangzhou, and captured Xu Kai.

sentences.zh: 進攻東昌，與盛庸軍遇。

translations.literal: Advancing to attack Dongchang, he met Sheng Yong's army.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing on Dongchang, he encountered Sheng Yong's army.

sentences.zh: 成祖以數十騎繞出其後。

translations.literal: Chengzu with several dozen horsemen circled behind them.
translations.idiomatic: The prince circled behind them with a few dozen horsemen.

sentences.zh: 庸圍之數重，成祖奮擊得出。

translations.literal: Yong surrounded him in many rings; Chengzu fought fiercely and broke out.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng Yong surrounded him in layer after layer, but the prince fought his way out.

sentences.zh: 玉不知成祖所在，突入陣中力戰，格殺數十人，被創死。

translations.literal: Yu did not know where Chengzu was; he plunged into the battle line and fought with all his strength, killing several dozen men in close combat, was wounded, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Not knowing where the prince was, Yu charged into the enemy ranks, killed dozens in hand-to-hand fighting, was wounded, and died.

sentences.zh: 年五十八。

translations.literal: He was fifty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He was fifty-eight years old.

sentences.zh: 子三人，長輔，次輗。

translations.literal: He had three sons: the eldest Fu, the second Yi.
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons: the eldest, Fu; the second, Yi.

sentences.zh: 次軏，從子信。

translations.literal: The third Yue; a nephew Xin.
translations.idiomatic: The third, Yue; and a nephew, Xin.

sentences.zh: 輔自有傳。

translations.literal: Fu has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Fu has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 子 輗等

translations.literal: Sons: Yi and others.
translations.idiomatic: The Sons: Yi and Others

sentences.zh: 輗，以功臣子為神策衛指揮使。

translations.literal: Yi, as son of a merit minister, was made commander of the Divine Strategy Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Yi, as the son of a meritorious minister, was appointed commander of the Divine Strategy Guard.

sentences.zh: 正統五年，英國公輔訴輗毆守墳者，斥及先臣，詞多悖慢。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhengtong, the Duke of Ying, Fu, accused Yi of beating tomb guardians, reviling his late father, with words mostly insolent and disrespectful.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Zhengtong the Duke of Ying, Fu, accused Yi of assaulting tomb guardians and speaking insolently of their late father.

sentences.zh: 帝命錦衣衛鞫實，錮之，尋釋。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered the Embroidered Uniform Guard to investigate the facts, imprisoned him, and soon released him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the Embroidered Uniform Guard to investigate, imprisoned him, and soon released him.

sentences.zh: 三遷至中府右都督，領宿衛。

translations.literal: After three promotions he reached Right Regional Commander of the Central Military Commission and led the palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: After three promotions he became Right Regional Commander of the Central Military Commission and commanded the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 景泰三年加太子太保。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jingtai he was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jingtai he was made Grand Guardian of the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 英宗復位，以軏迎立功，並封輗文安伯，食祿千二百石。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ying was restored, because Yue had merited service in welcoming him, Yi was also enfeoffed as Marquis of Wen'an with an income of twelve hundred piculs.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ying was restored, Yi was enfeoffed as Marquis of Wen'an with an income of twelve hundred piculs, sharing in the credit for Yue's role in the restoration.

sentences.zh: 天順六年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the sixth year of Tianshun.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixth year of Tianshun.

sentences.zh: 贈侯，謚忠僖。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made a marquis, posthumous title Zhongxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made a marquis with the posthumous name Zhongxi.

sentences.zh: 子斌嗣，坐詛咒，奪爵。

translations.literal: His son Bin succeeded; for cursing he was deprived of the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Bin succeeded him but was stripped of the title for sorcery.

sentences.zh: 信，舉建文二年鄉試第一。

translations.literal: Xin placed first in the provincial examination of the second year of Jianwen.
translations.idiomatic: Xin placed first in the provincial examinations of the second year of Jianwen.

sentences.zh: 永樂中，歷刑科都給事中，數言事。

translations.literal: In the Yongle period he served through as supervising secretary of the Penal Branch, repeatedly memorializing on affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yongle he rose to supervising secretary of the Penal Branch and frequently memorialized the throne.

sentences.zh: 擢工部右侍郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 奉命視開封決河，請疏魚王口至中灤故道二十餘里。

translations.literal: Ordered to inspect the Yellow River breach at Kaifeng, he requested dredging the old channel from Yuwang Mouth to Zhongluan, more than twenty li.
translations.idiomatic: Commissioned to inspect the Yellow River breach at Kaifeng, he proposed reopening the old channel from Yuwang Mouth to Zhongluan, more than twenty li in length.

sentences.zh: 詔如其議，詳《宋禮傳》。

translations.literal: An edict followed his proposal; see the biography of Song Li.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved his plan; see the biography of Song Li for details.

sentences.zh: 出治浙江海塘，坐事謫交阯。

translations.literal: Sent out to manage Zhejiang's sea dikes, he was demoted to Jiaozhi for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: Sent to repair Zhejiang's sea dikes, he was banished to Jiaozhi for an offense.

sentences.zh: 洪熙初，召為兵部左侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Hongxi he was recalled as Left Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Hongxi reign he was recalled as Left Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗謂英國公輔：「有兄弟可加恩者乎？

translations.literal: The Emperor once said to the Duke of Ying, Fu, "Are there brothers who can be shown favor?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once asked the Duke of Ying, Fu, "Are there brothers of yours who deserve favor?

sentences.zh: 」輔頓首言：「輗、軏蒙上恩，備近侍，然皆奢侈。

translations.literal: " Fu bowed his head and said, "Yi and Yue have received the Emperor's grace and serve in close attendance, yet both are extravagant.
translations.idiomatic: Fu kowtowed and replied, "Yi and Yue have enjoyed Your Majesty's grace as palace attendants, but both are extravagant.

sentences.zh: 獨從兄侍郎信賢，可使也。

translations.literal: Only my cousin, Vice Minister Xin, is worthy—he may be employed.
translations.idiomatic: Only my cousin, Vice Minister Xin, is worthy of trust.

sentences.zh: 」帝召見信曰：「是英國公兄耶？

translations.literal: " The Emperor summoned Xin and said, "Are you the Duke of Ying's elder brother?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Xin and asked, "Are you the Duke of Ying's elder cousin?

sentences.zh: 」趣武冠冠之，改錦衣衛指揮同知，世襲。

translations.literal: " He hurriedly had him capped with a military cap, changed his post to Vice Commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard, hereditary.
translations.idiomatic: He had a military cap placed on his head at once, appointed him Vice Commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard, and made the post hereditary.

sentences.zh: 時去開國未遠，武階重故也。

translations.literal: The time was not far from the founding, and military rank was therefore valued.
translations.idiomatic: The founding was still recent, and military rank still carried great weight.

sentences.zh: 居職以平恕稱。

translations.literal: In office he was known for fairness and clemency.
translations.idiomatic: In office he was known for fairness and leniency.

sentences.zh: 宣德六年遷四川都指揮僉事。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Xuande he was transferred to assistant regional commander of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Xuande he was transferred to assistant regional commander of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 在蜀十五年致仕。

translations.literal: After fifteen years in Shu he retired.
translations.idiomatic: After fifteen years in Sichuan he retired.

sentences.zh: 朱能，字士弘，懷遠人。

translations.literal: Zhu Neng, styled Shihong, was a man of Huaiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Neng, styled Shihong, was a native of Huaiyuan.

sentences.zh: 父亮，從太祖渡江，積功至燕山護衛副千戶。

translations.literal: His father Liang followed the Founding Emperor in crossing the Yangzi, accumulated merit to vice thousand-household of the Yan Mountain Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His father Liang had followed the Hongwu Emperor across the Yangzi and risen to vice thousand-household of the Yan Mountain Guard.

sentences.zh: 能嗣職，事成祖藩邸。

translations.literal: Neng succeeded to the post and served in Chengzu's princely residence.
translations.idiomatic: Neng inherited the post and served in the prince's household.

sentences.zh: 嘗從北征，降元太尉乃兒不花。

translations.literal: He once followed the northern campaign and received the surrender of the Yuan Grand Preceptor Nayir Buqa.
translations.idiomatic: On a northern campaign he accepted the surrender of the Yuan Grand Preceptor Nayir Buqa.

sentences.zh: 燕兵起，與張玉首謀殺張昺、謝貴，奪九門。

translations.literal: When the Yan army rose, with Zhang Yu he first plotted to kill Zhang Bing and Xie Gui and seize the nine gates.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebellion began, he and Zhang Yu first plotted to kill Zhang Bing and Xie Gui and seize the nine gates.

sentences.zh: 授指揮同知。

translations.literal: He was appointed vice commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed vice commander.

sentences.zh: 帥眾拔薊州，殺馬宣，下遵化。

translations.literal: Leading the host he took Jizhou, killed Ma Xuan, and reduced Zunhua.
translations.idiomatic: He led the troops to take Jizhou, kill Ma Xuan, and secure Zunhua.

sentences.zh: 從破雄縣，戰月漾橋，執楊松、潘忠，降其眾於鄚州。

translations.literal: He followed in breaking Xiong County, fought at Yueyang Bridge, seized Yang Song and Pan Zhong, and reduced their forces at Mozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He helped storm Xiong County, fought at Yueyang Bridge, captured Yang Song and Pan Zhong, and accepted the surrender of their troops at Mozhou.

sentences.zh: 長驅至真定，大敗耿炳文軍。

translations.literal: He drove straight to Zhending and routed Geng Bingwen's army.
translations.idiomatic: He marched straight to Zhending and routed Geng Bingwen's army.

sentences.zh: 獨與敢死士三十騎追奔至滹沱河，躍馬大呼突南軍，軍數萬人皆披靡，蹂藉死者甚眾，降三千余人。

translations.literal: Alone with thirty dare-to-die horsemen he pursued the fugitives to the Hutuo River, leaped his horse, shouted greatly, and charged the southern army; an army of tens of thousands all crumbled; trampled and crushed, the dead were very many; more than three thousand surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: With only thirty daredevil horsemen he pursued the fugitives to the Hutuo River, spurred his horse forward with a great shout, and charged the southern army of tens of thousands, which broke and fled; countless were trampled to death, and more than three thousand surrendered.

sentences.zh: 成祖以手劄勞之，進都指揮僉事。

translations.literal: Chengzu with a personal letter commended him and promoted him to assistant regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: The prince commended him in a personal letter and promoted him to assistant regional commander.

sentences.zh: 從援永平，走吳高，襲克大寧。

translations.literal: He followed in relieving Yongping, drove off Wu Gao, and raided to take Daning.
translations.idiomatic: He helped relieve Yongping, drove off Wu Gao, and took Daning by surprise.

sentences.zh: 還，將左軍，破李景隆於鄭村壩。

translations.literal: On return he commanded the left army and defeated Li Jinglong at Zhengcun Dam.
translations.idiomatic: On the return march he commanded the left army and defeated Li Jinglong at Zhengcun Dam.

sentences.zh: 從攻廣昌、蔚州、大同，戰白溝河，為前鋒，再敗平安軍。

translations.literal: He followed attacks on Guangchang, Yuzhou, and Datong, fought at the White Ditch River as vanguard, and again defeated Ping'an's army.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned at Guangchang, Yuzhou, and Datong, fought at the White Ditch River as vanguard, and twice defeated Ping'an's army.

sentences.zh: 進攻濟南，次鏵山。

translations.literal: Advancing to attack Jinan, he encamped at Huashan.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing on Jinan, he encamped at Huashan.

sentences.zh: 南軍乘高而陣，能以奇兵繞其後，襲破之，降萬余人。

translations.literal: The southern army drew up on high ground; Neng with odd troops circled behind them, raided and broke them, and more than ten thousand surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: When the southern army drew up on the heights, he sent a flanking force around their rear, routed them, and accepted the surrender of more than ten thousand men.

sentences.zh: 從攻滄州，破東門入，斬首萬余級。

translations.literal: He followed the attack on Cangzhou, broke through the east gate and entered, and cut off more than ten thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: At Cangzhou he broke through the east gate and slew more than ten thousand men.

sentences.zh: 東昌之戰，盛庸、鐵鉉圍成祖數重。

translations.literal: In the battle of Dongchang, Sheng Yong and Tie Xuan surrounded Chengzu in many rings.
translations.idiomatic: At the battle of Dongchang, Sheng Yong and Tie Xuan surrounded the prince in layer after layer.

sentences.zh: 張玉戰死。

translations.literal: Zhang Yu died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yu was killed in battle.

sentences.zh: 事急，能帥周長等殊死鬥，翼成祖潰圍出。

translations.literal: As matters grew urgent, Neng led Zhou Chang and others in a fight to the death, assisting Chengzu to break out of the encirclement.
translations.idiomatic: When the situation grew desperate, Neng led Zhou Chang and others in a desperate fight and helped the prince break out of the encirclement.

sentences.zh: 復從戰夾河，譚淵死，燕師挫。

translations.literal: Again he followed to fight at Jiahe; Tan Yuan died; the Yan army was thwarted.
translations.idiomatic: He fought again at Jiahe, where Tan Yuan was killed and the Yan army suffered a setback.

sentences.zh: 能至，再戰再捷，軍復振。

translations.literal: When Neng arrived, again he fought and again he was victorious; the army recovered its morale.
translations.idiomatic: When Neng arrived, he won battle after battle and the army's spirits revived.

sentences.zh: 與平安戰槁城，敗之。

translations.literal: He fought Ping'an at Gaocheng and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: He fought Ping'an at Gaocheng and defeated him.

sentences.zh: 追奔至真定，略地彰德、定州，破西水寨。

translations.literal: Pursuing fugitives to Zhending, he seized territory at Zhangde and Dingzhou and broke the West Water stockade.
translations.idiomatic: He pursued the fleeing enemy to Zhending, seized territory in Zhangde and Dingzhou, and stormed the West Water stockade.

sentences.zh: 將輕騎千人掠衡水，獲指揮賈榮。

translations.literal: Leading a thousand light horsemen he raided Hengshui and captured Commander Jia Rong.
translations.idiomatic: At the head of a thousand light cavalry he raided Hengshui and captured Commander Jia Rong.

sentences.zh: 克東阿、東平，盡破汶上諸寨。

translations.literal: He took Dong'e and Dongping and completely broke all the stockades at Wenshang.
translations.idiomatic: He captured Dong'e and Dongping and swept away all the stockades around Wenshang.

sentences.zh: 既而王真戰死淝河，燕軍屢敗。

translations.literal: Before long Wang Zhen died in battle at the Fei River and the Yan army suffered repeated defeats.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Wang Zhen was killed in battle at the Fei River, and the Yan army suffered defeat after defeat.

sentences.zh: 諸將議旋師，能獨按劍曰：「漢高十戰九敗，終有天下。

translations.literal: The generals discussed turning back the army; Neng alone, hand on sword, said: "Emperor Gaozu of Han lost nine out of ten battles yet in the end possessed the realm under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: When the generals talked of withdrawing, Neng alone gripped his sword and said, "Emperor Gaozu of Han lost nine battles out of ten, yet in the end he won the empire.

sentences.zh: 今舉事連得勝。

translations.literal: Now our enterprise has won victory after victory.
translations.idiomatic: Our cause has won victory after victory.

sentences.zh: 小挫輒歸，更能北面事人耶！

translations.literal: At a small setback you would return — can one after that still face north and serve others!
translations.idiomatic: Are we to turn back at the first setback and then go north again to serve another master?

sentences.zh: 」成祖亦叱諸將曰：「任公等所之！

translations.literal: " Chengzu also shouted at the generals: "Do as you please, gentlemen!
translations.idiomatic: " The prince also shouted at his generals, "Go wherever you like, gentlemen!

sentences.zh: 」諸將乃不敢言。

translations.literal: " The generals then did not dare speak.
translations.idiomatic: " The generals then fell silent.

sentences.zh: 遂引兵南，敗平安銀牌軍。

translations.literal: Thereupon he led the army south and defeated Ping'an's Silver Plaque army.
translations.idiomatic: He then marched south and defeated Ping'an's Silver Plaque army.

sentences.zh: 都督陳暉來援，又敗之。

translations.literal: Regional commander Chen Hui came to the rescue and again he was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Regional Commander Chen Hui came to the rescue, and Neng defeated him as well.

sentences.zh: 遂拔靈璧軍，擒平安等，降十萬眾。

translations.literal: Thereupon he took Lingbi's army, captured Ping'an and others, and reduced one hundred thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: He then captured the army at Lingbi, seized Ping'an and others, and accepted the surrender of one hundred thousand troops.

sentences.zh: 累遷右軍都督僉事。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to assistant commander of the Right Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to assistant regional commander in the Right Army.

sentences.zh: 進克泗州，渡淮，敗盛庸兵。

translations.literal: Advancing he took Sizhou, crossed the Huai, and defeated Sheng Yong's troops.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced to take Sizhou, crossed the Huai River, and defeated Sheng Yong's army.

sentences.zh: 拔盱眙，下揚州，渡江，入金川門。

translations.literal: He took Xuyi, reduced Yangzhou, crossed the river, and entered Jinchuan Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He captured Xuyi, took Yangzhou, crossed the Yangtze, and entered the capital through Jinchuan Gate.

sentences.zh: 九月甲申論功，次邱福。

translations.literal: On jiashen day of the ninth month merits were reckoned; he ranked next after Qiu Fu.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiashen day of the ninth month the prince rewarded his generals; Neng ranked second only to Qiu Fu.

sentences.zh: 授奉天靖難推誠宣力武臣、特進榮祿大夫、右柱國、左軍都督府左都督，封成國公，祿二千二百石，與世券。

translations.literal: He was appointed Martial Merit lord of the Fengtian Jingnan campaign who extends sincerity and deploys strength, specially promoted Grand Master of Glorious Emolument, Pillar of the State of the Second Rank, left regional commander of the Left Army Directorate, enfeoffed as Duke of the State of Cheng, salary two thousand two hundred shi, with a hereditary warrant.
translations.idiomatic: He was made a fengtian jingnan merit lord, specially promoted to Grand Master of Glorious Emolument, given the second-rank title Pillar of the State, appointed left regional commander of the Left Army Directorate, enfeoffed as Duke of Cheng, granted an annual stipend of 2,200 shi, and awarded a hereditary warrant of protection.

sentences.zh: 永樂二年兼太子太傅，加祿千石。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongle he concurrently served as Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent and received an additional salary of one thousand shi.
translations.idiomatic: In 1404 he was made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent and granted an additional 1,000 shi per year.

sentences.zh: 四年七月詔能佩征夷將軍印，西平侯沐晟為左副將軍，由廣西、雲南分道討安南，帝親送之龍江。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the fourth year an edict ordered Neng to wear the seal of the General Who Pacifies the Yi; the Marquis of Xiping Mu Sheng served as left deputy general; by separate routes from Guangxi and Yunnan they would chastise Annan; the emperor personally saw them off at Longjiang.
translations.idiomatic: In July 1406 the emperor ordered Neng to take the seal of General Who Pacifies the Barbarians, with the Marquis of Xiping, Mu Sheng, as his deputy; they were to invade Annam by separate routes through Guangxi and Yunnan, and the emperor personally saw them off at Longjiang.

sentences.zh: 十月行次龍州，卒於軍。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, marching and stopping at Longzhou, he died in the army.
translations.idiomatic: In October, while the army was encamped at Longzhou, he died on campaign.

sentences.zh: 年三十七。

translations.literal: His age was thirty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He was thirty-seven years old.

sentences.zh: 能於諸將中年最少，善戰，張玉善謀，帝倚為左右手。

translations.literal: Among the generals Neng was the youngest in years, skilled in battle; Zhang Yu was skilled in planning; the emperor relied on the two as his left and right hands.
translations.idiomatic: Neng was the youngest of the leading generals and excelled in battle, while Zhang Yu excelled in strategy; the emperor relied on both as his right and left hands.

sentences.zh: 玉歿後，軍中進止悉諮能。

translations.literal: After Yu died, all advances and halts in the army were entirely consulted with Neng.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhang Yu's death, every movement of the army was decided on Neng's advice.

sentences.zh: 能身長八尺。

translations.literal: Neng's body length was eight chi.
translations.idiomatic: Neng stood eight chi tall.

sentences.zh: 雄毅開豁，居家孝友。

translations.literal: Heroic and resolute, open and magnanimous, at home he was filial and fraternal.
translations.idiomatic: Heroic and open-hearted by nature, he was filial and devoted to his family at home.

sentences.zh: 位列上公，未嘗以富貴驕人。

translations.literal: His rank stood among the highest nobles; he never used wealth and honor to be arrogant toward others.
translations.idiomatic: Though he stood among the highest nobility, he never let rank and wealth make him arrogant toward others.

sentences.zh: 善撫士卒。

translations.literal: He was skilled in comforting and governing soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: He treated his soldiers with great kindness.

sentences.zh: 卒之日，將校皆為流涕。

translations.literal: On the day of his death, officers and commanders all shed tears for him.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, officers and commanders throughout the ranks wept.

sentences.zh: 敕葬昌平，追封東平王，謚武烈。

translations.literal: An edict ordered burial at Changping; posthumously he was enfeoffed as Prince of Dongping; his posthumous title was Wulie.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered him buried at Changping, posthumously enfeoffed him as Prince of Dongping, and granted him the posthumous title Wulie, "Fierce in War."

sentences.zh: 洪熙時，配享成祖廟廷。

translations.literal: In the Hongxi reign he was granted accompanying sacrifice in Chengzu's temple court.
translations.idiomatic: In the Hongxi reign he was granted a place in the sacrifices at the temple of the Chengzu emperor.

sentences.zh: 勇赪面虬須，狀貌甚偉，勇略不足，而敬禮士大夫。

translations.literal: Yong had a red face and curly whiskers; his form and appearance were very grand; courage and strategy were insufficient, yet he respectfully honored scholar-officials.
translations.idiomatic: Yong had a ruddy face and curling whiskers and cut a towering figure, but he lacked courage and strategic skill—though he was always respectful toward the scholar-official class.

sentences.zh: 十四年從駕至土木，迎戰鷂兒嶺，中伏死，所帥五萬騎皆沒。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he followed the emperor to Tumu; he met the enemy in battle at Yao'er Ridge; hit by an ambush he died; the fifty thousand horsemen he commanded all perished.
translations.idiomatic: In 1449 he accompanied the emperor to Tumu, met the Mongols in battle at Yao'er Ridge, and was killed in an ambush along with all fifty thousand cavalry under his command.

sentences.zh: 于謙等追論勇罪，奪封。

translations.literal: Yu Qian and others retroactively judged Yong's crimes and stripped his enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Qian and others reviewed Yong's crimes and stripped him of his title.

sentences.zh: 景泰元年，勇子儀乞葬祭。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingtai, Yong's son Yi begged for burial rites and sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In 1450 Yong's son Yi petitioned for permission to bury his father and perform sacrificial rites.

sentences.zh: 帝以勇大將，喪師辱國，致陷乘輿，不許。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Yong was a great general who lost the army and disgraced the state, causing the imperial carriage to be trapped, did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused, on the grounds that Yong, as a senior commander, had lost his army, shamed the empire, and brought about the emperor's capture.

sentences.zh: 已，請襲。

translations.literal: Already afterward, he requested inheritance of the title.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yi petitioned to inherit his father's title.

sentences.zh: 禮部尚書胡濙主之，又以立東宮恩得嗣，減歲祿至千石。

translations.literal: Minister of Rites Hu Ying chaired the deliberation; also, through the grace of establishing the Eastern Palace, he obtained succession; the yearly salary was reduced to one thousand shi.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Rites Hu Ying supported the petition, and Yi was permitted to inherit the title owing to the grace shown when the Eastern Palace was established, though his annual stipend was reduced to 1,000 shi.

sentences.zh: 天順初，追封勇平陰王，謚武湣。

translations.literal: At the start of Tianshun he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Pingyin; his posthumous title was Wumin.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Tianshun reign Yong was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Pingyin with the posthumous title Wumin, "Warlike and Lamentable."

sentences.zh: 儀及子輔皆守備南京。

translations.literal: Yi and his son Fu both served as defenders of Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Yi and his son Fu both served as commanders of the Nanjing garrison.

sentences.zh: 又三傳至希忠，從世宗幸承天，掌行在左府事。

translations.literal: After three more generations it passed to Xizhong; he followed Shizong on a visit to Chengtian and managed affairs of the Left Directorate at the mobile court.
translations.idiomatic: Three generations later the line reached Xizhong, who accompanied the Jiajing emperor on a visit to Chengtian and administered affairs of the Left Military Directorate at the traveling court.

sentences.zh: 至衛輝，行宮夜火，希忠與都督陸炳翼帝出，由是被恩遇，入直西苑。

translations.literal: Reaching Weihui, at night fire broke out in the traveling palace; Xizhong and regional commander Lu Bing assisted the emperor out; thereby he received favored treatment and entered service in the Western Park.
translations.idiomatic: At Weihui a fire broke out in the traveling palace at night; Xizhong and Regional Commander Lu Bing helped the emperor to safety, and from then on he enjoyed the emperor's special favor and entered service in the Western Park.

sentences.zh: 歷掌後、右兩府，總神機營，提督十二團營及五軍營，累加太師，益歲祿七百石。

translations.literal: He successively managed the Rear and Right directorates, commanded the Divine Engine camp, supervised the twelve regiment camps and the Five Armies camp, was repeatedly promoted to Grand Preceptor, and received an increase of seven hundred shi yearly salary.
translations.idiomatic: He successively commanded the Rear and Right Military Directorates, oversaw the Divine Engine Corps and the twelve regiment camps and Five Armies camps, was repeatedly promoted to Grand Preceptor, and received an additional stipend of 700 shi per year.

sentences.zh: 代郊天者三十九，賞賚不可勝紀。

translations.literal: As substitute at suburban heaven rites, thirty-nine times; rewards and gifts cannot all be recorded.
translations.idiomatic: He stood in for the emperor at thirty-nine suburban sacrifices to Heaven, and the rewards he received were beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 卒，追封定襄王，謚恭靖。

translations.literal: At his death he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Dingxiang; his posthumous title was Gongjing.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Dingxiang with the posthumous title Gongjing, "Respectful and Tranquil."

sentences.zh: 萬歷十一年，以給事中余懋學言，追奪王爵。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Wanli, on the remonstrance of supervising secretary Yu Maoxue, his princely title was retroactively stripped.
translations.idiomatic: In 1583, on the memorial of supervising secretary Yu Maoxue, his princely title was posthumously revoked.

sentences.zh: 弟希孝亦至都督，加太保。

translations.literal: His younger brother Xixiao also rose to regional commander and received the added title of Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Xixiao also rose to regional commander and was made Grand Guardian.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈太傅，謚忠僖。

translations.literal: At death he was posthumously given Grand Mentor; his posthumous title was Zhongxi.
translations.idiomatic: After his death he was posthumously made Grand Mentor with the posthumous title Zhongxi, "Loyal and Gentle."

sentences.zh: 希忠五傳至曾孫純臣，崇禎時見倚任。

translations.literal: From Xizhong, after five transmissions it reached his great-grandson Chunchen; in the Chongzhen era he was seen to be relied upon and entrusted.
translations.idiomatic: Five generations after Xizhong the line reached his great-great-grandson Chunchen, who in the Chongzhen reign was highly trusted by the throne.

sentences.zh: 李自成薄京師，帝手刺純臣總督中外諸軍，輔太子。

translations.literal: Li Zicheng pressed close to the capital; the emperor with his own hand wrote an edict appointing Chunchen to oversee all armies at home and abroad and assist the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Zicheng closed in on Beijing, the emperor personally wrote orders naming Chunchen supreme commander of all armies within and beyond the capital and assistant to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 敕未下，城已陷，為賊所殺。

translations.literal: Before the edict was issued, the city had already fallen; he was killed by bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Before the order could be issued the city had already fallen, and he was killed by the rebels.

sentences.zh: 邱福，鳳陽人。

translations.literal: Qiu Fu was a man of Fengyang.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Fu was a native of Fengyang.

sentences.zh: 起卒伍，事成祖藩邸。

translations.literal: He rose from the ranks of conscript soldiers and served in Chengzu's princely residence.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from the ranks and served in the prince of Yan's household.

sentences.zh: 積年勞，授燕山中護衛千戶。

translations.literal: Accumulating years of labor, he was appointed chiliarch of the Yan Mountain Bodyguard.
translations.idiomatic: After years of service he was made a chiliarch in the prince's bodyguard.

sentences.zh: 燕師起，與朱能、張玉首奪九門。

translations.literal: When the Yan army rose, with Zhu Neng and Zhang Yu he was first to seize the nine gates.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yan army rose in rebellion, he was among the first, with Zhu Neng and Zhang Yu, to seize the nine gates of Beijing.

sentences.zh: 大戰真定，突入子城。

translations.literal: In the great battle at Zhending he burst into the inner city.
translations.idiomatic: At the great battle of Zhending he broke into the inner city.

sentences.zh: 戰白溝河，以勁卒搗中堅。

translations.literal: At the battle of the White Ditch River he with crack troops struck the center.
translations.idiomatic: At the White Ditch River he led crack troops in a thrust against the enemy center.

sentences.zh: 夾河、滄州、靈璧諸大戰，皆為軍鋒。

translations.literal: At Jiahe, Cangzhou, Lingbi, and other great battles, he all served as the army's spear point.
translations.idiomatic: At Jiahe, Cangzhou, Lingbi, and other major engagements he always served at the head of the army.

sentences.zh: 盛庸兵扼淮，戰艦數千艘蔽淮岸。

translations.literal: Sheng Yong's troops blocked the Huai; several thousand warships covered the Huai shore.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng Yong's army held the Huai River line, with thousands of warships crowding the riverbank.

sentences.zh: 福與朱能將數百人，西行二十里，自上流潛濟，猝薄南軍。

translations.literal: Fu and Zhu Neng led several hundred men, marched west twenty li, secretly crossed from the upper reaches, and suddenly pressed close to the southern army.
translations.idiomatic: Fu and Zhu Neng took several hundred men twenty li upstream, crossed the river in secret, and suddenly fell upon the southern army.

sentences.zh: 庸驚走，盡奪其戰艦，軍乃得渡。

translations.literal: Yong fled in alarm; they completely seized his warships; the army then was able to cross.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng Yong fled in panic; they captured his entire fleet, and the Yan army was able to cross the river.

sentences.zh: 累遷至中軍都督同知。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to vice regional commander of the Central Army.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through repeated promotions to vice regional commander of the Central Army.

sentences.zh: 福為人樸戇鷙勇，謀畫智計不如玉，敢戰深入與能埒。

translations.literal: Fu as a man was plain, blunt, fierce and brave; in planning and stratagem he was not the equal of Yu; in daring to fight and penetrate deeply he was on a par with Neng.
translations.idiomatic: Fu was plainspoken, blunt, and ferocious in battle; he could not match Zhang Yu in strategy, but in bold charges and deep pursuit he was the equal of Zhu Neng.

sentences.zh: 每戰勝，諸將爭前效虜獲，福獨後。

translations.literal: Each time he won in battle, the generals vied to go forward and present captives and booty; Fu alone came behind.
translations.idiomatic: After every victory the other generals raced forward to present captives and booty, but Fu always held back.

sentences.zh: 成祖每嘆曰：「丘將軍功，我自知之。

translations.literal: Chengzu every time sighed and said: "General Qiu's merit — I myself know it.
translations.idiomatic: The prince often sighed and said, "General Qiu's achievements—I know them well myself.

sentences.zh: 」即位，大封功臣，第福為首。

translations.literal: " On taking the throne, in the great enfeoffment of merit lords, Fu was ranked first.
translations.idiomatic: " After ascending the throne he enfeoffed his merit lords, ranking Fu first among them all.

sentences.zh: 授奉天靖難推誠宣力武臣、特進榮祿大夫、右柱國、中軍都督府左都督，封淇國公，祿二千五百石，與世券。

translations.literal: He was appointed Martial Merit lord of the Fengtian Jingnan campaign who extends sincerity and deploys strength, specially promoted Grand Master of Glorious Emolument, Pillar of the State of the Second Rank, left regional commander of the Central Army Directorate, enfeoffed as Duke of the State of Qi, salary two thousand five hundred shi, with a hereditary warrant.
translations.idiomatic: He was made a fengtian jingnan merit lord, specially promoted to Grand Master of Glorious Emolument, given the second-rank title Pillar of the State, appointed left regional commander of the Central Army Directorate, enfeoffed as Duke of Qi, granted an annual stipend of 2,500 shi, and awarded a hereditary warrant of protection.

sentences.zh: 命議諸功臣封賞，每奉命議政，皆首福。

translations.literal: Ordered to deliberate on the enfeoffments and rewards of the merit lords, each time he received orders to discuss state affairs, Fu always came first.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the court deliberated on rewards for the merit lords or on matters of state, Fu was always listed first.

sentences.zh: 漢王高煦數將兵有功，成祖愛之。

translations.literal: The Prince of Han, Gao Xu, several times led troops with merit; Chengzu loved him.
translations.idiomatic: The prince of Han, Zhu Gaoxu, had repeatedly led troops to victory, and Chengzu favored him.

sentences.zh: 福武人，與之善，數勸立為太子。

translations.literal: Fu was a military man; he was on good terms with him and several times urged that he be established as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Fu, a military man, was on close terms with Gaoxu and repeatedly urged the emperor to make him crown prince.

sentences.zh: 帝猶豫久之，竟立仁宗。

translations.literal: The emperor hesitated for a long time but in the end established Renzong as heir.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wavered for a long time but ultimately established the heir who would become the Renzong emperor.

sentences.zh: 以福為太子太師。

translations.literal: Fu was made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Fu was appointed Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 六年加歲祿千石。

translations.literal: In the sixth year his yearly salary was increased by one thousand shi.
translations.idiomatic: In 1408 his annual stipend was increased by 1,000 shi.

sentences.zh: 尋命與蹇義、金忠等輔導皇長孫。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered with Jian Yi, Jin Zhong, and others to assist and instruct the eldest imperial grandson.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was ordered, together with Jian Yi, Jin Zhong, and others, to tutor the emperor's eldest grandson.

sentences.zh: 明年七月將大軍出塞，至臚朐河，敗沒。

translations.literal: The next year in the seventh month he led a great army beyond the passes; reaching the Lulut River, he was defeated and destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: The following July he led a major army beyond the frontier; at the Lulut River his force was annihilated.

sentences.zh: 先是，本雅失裏殺使臣郭驥，帝大怒，發兵討之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Benyashiri killed the envoy Guo Ji; the emperor was greatly angered and sent troops to chastise him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the Mongol leader Benyashiri had killed the envoy Guo Ji, and the emperor, furious, launched a punitive campaign.

sentences.zh: 命福佩征虜大將軍印，充總兵官。

translations.literal: Fu was ordered to wear the seal of the Great General Who Conquers the Barbarians and to serve as overall commander.
translations.idiomatic: Fu was ordered to take the seal of Great General Who Conquers the Barbarians and serve as supreme commander.

sentences.zh: 武城侯王聰、同安侯火真為左、右副將，靖安侯王忠、安平侯李遠為左、右參將，以十萬騎行。

translations.literal: The Marquis of Wucheng Wang Cong and the Marquis of Tong'an Huo Zhen served as left and right deputy generals; the Marquis of Jing'an Wang Zhong and the Marquis of Anping Li Yuan served as left and right staff generals; they marched with one hundred thousand horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: The Marquis of Wucheng Wang Cong and the Marquis of Tong'an Huo Zhen served as his deputies, the Marquis of Jing'an Wang Zhong and the Marquis of Anping Li Yuan as staff generals, and the army marched with one hundred thousand cavalry.

sentences.zh: 帝慮福輕敵，諭以：「兵事須慎重。

translations.literal: The emperor feared Fu would underestimate the enemy and instructed him: "Military matters must be careful and weighty.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing that Fu would underestimate the enemy, the emperor instructed him: "Military affairs demand the utmost caution.

sentences.zh: 自開平以北，即不見寇。

translations.literal: From north of Kaiping onward, if you do not encounter the enemy,
translations.idiomatic: From Kaiping northward, if you do not see the enemy,

sentences.zh: 宜時時如對敵，相機進止，不可執一。

translations.literal: you should at every moment act as though facing the enemy, advancing or halting according to opportunity — you must not cling to one fixed [plan].
translations.idiomatic: you must always act as if the enemy were before you, advancing or holding back as circumstances require, and never cling stubbornly to one approach.

sentences.zh: 一舉未捷，俟再舉。

translations.literal: If one attempt does not succeed, wait for another attempt.
translations.idiomatic: If the first strike fails, wait and strike again.

sentences.zh: 」已行，又連賜敕，謂軍中有言敵易取者，慎勿信之。

translations.literal: " After he had marched, the emperor again repeatedly granted edicts, saying that if in the army there were words that the enemy was easy to take, carefully do not believe them.
translations.idiomatic: " After the army had marched, the emperor sent a series of edicts warning that if anyone in the ranks said the enemy would be easy to defeat, Fu must on no account believe it.

sentences.zh: 福出塞，帥千余人先至臚朐河南。

translations.literal: Fu went beyond the passes; leading more than a thousand men he first reached the south of the Lulut River.
translations.idiomatic: Fu crossed the frontier and, leading more than a thousand men, reached the south bank of the Lulut River ahead of the main force.

sentences.zh: 遇遊騎，擊敗之，遂渡河。

translations.literal: He encountered roaming horsemen, struck and defeated them, and thereupon crossed the river.
translations.idiomatic: He encountered enemy scouts, routed them, and crossed the river.

sentences.zh: 獲其尚書一人，飲之酒，問本雅失裏所在。

translations.literal: He captured one of their grand secretaries, gave him wine to drink, and asked where Benyashiri was.
translations.idiomatic: He captured a Mongol minister, gave him wine, and asked where Benyashiri was.

sentences.zh: 尚書言：「聞大兵來，惶恐北走，去此可三十里。

translations.literal: The grand secretary said: "Hearing that the great army is coming, [he] in fear fled north; from here it is about thirty li.
translations.idiomatic: The minister said, "When he heard the great army was coming he fled north in terror; he is about thirty li from here.

sentences.zh: 」福大喜曰：「當疾馳擒之。

translations.literal: " Fu greatly rejoiced and said: "We should speed our horses to capture him.
translations.idiomatic: " Fu was overjoyed and said, "We must ride hard and capture him at once.

sentences.zh: 」諸將請俟諸軍集，偵虛實而後進。

translations.literal: " The generals requested to wait until all armies had assembled, reconnoiter the real situation, and then advance.
translations.idiomatic: " The other generals urged him to wait for the main army to assemble, scout the enemy's strength, and then advance.

sentences.zh: 福不從。

translations.literal: Fu did not follow [their advice].
translations.idiomatic: Fu refused.

sentences.zh: 以尚書為鄉導，直薄敵營。

translations.literal: Taking the grand secretary as local guide, he pressed straight at the enemy camp.
