translations.idiomatic: Using the minister as his guide, he pressed straight into the enemy camp.

sentences.zh: 戰二日，每戰，敵輒佯敗引去，福銳意乘之。

translations.literal: They fought for two days; each time they fought, the enemy always feigned defeat and drew away; Fu was keen to pursue and take advantage.
translations.idiomatic: For two days they fought; each time the enemy feigned retreat, and Fu eagerly pressed the pursuit.

sentences.zh: 李遠諫曰：「將軍輕信敵閑，懸軍轉鬥。

translations.literal: Li Yuan remonstrated, saying: "General, you lightly believe the enemy's idle talk and with a detached army turn and fight repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuan remonstrated: "General, you have too readily believed the enemy's disinformation and are fighting on and on with an isolated force.

sentences.zh: 敵示弱誘我深入，進必不利，退則懼為所乘，獨可結營自固。

translations.literal: The enemy shows weakness to lure us deep; advancing will certainly be unbeneficial; retreating then fears being seized by them; only by making camp and securing oneself [can we hold].
translations.idiomatic: They are feigning weakness to lure us deeper; to advance will bring disaster, and to retreat risks being overrun. We should encamp and hold our ground.

sentences.zh: 晝揚旗伐鼓，出奇兵與挑戰；

translations.literal: By day raise flags and beat drums, send out odd troops to skirmish and challenge;
translations.idiomatic: By day we should fly banners and beat drums, send out flanking detachments to skirmish and provoke them;

sentences.zh: 夜多燃炬鳴炮，張軍勢，使彼莫測。

translations.literal: by night often burn many torches and fire cannon, display military power, and make them unable to fathom [us].
translations.idiomatic: by night burn torches and fire cannon to display our strength and keep the enemy guessing.

sentences.zh: 俟我軍畢至，併力攻之，必捷。

translations.literal: Wait until our army has all arrived, combine strength to attack them, and victory is certain.
translations.idiomatic: Wait until our full force arrives, then strike with combined strength — we are sure to prevail.

sentences.zh: 否，亦可全師而還。

translations.literal: If not, we can still preserve the army intact and return.
translations.idiomatic: If not, we can still withdraw with the army intact.

sentences.zh: 始上與將軍言何如，而遂忘之乎？

translations.literal: At the beginning, what did the emperor say to the general, and yet you have forgotten it?
translations.idiomatic: What did His Majesty tell you at the outset, General — and have you forgotten it already?

sentences.zh: 」王聰亦力言不可。

translations.literal: " Wang Cong also forcefully argued that it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Cong also argued strenuously against it.

sentences.zh: 福皆不聽，厲聲曰：「違命者斬！

translations.literal: Fu would listen to none of them and said in a harsh voice: "Whoever disobeys orders shall be beheaded!
translations.idiomatic: Fu refused to heed any of them and shouted, "Whoever disobeys orders will be executed!

sentences.zh: 」即先馳，麾士卒隨行。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he galloped ahead first and waved the soldiers to follow.
translations.idiomatic: " Then he spurred ahead and ordered the troops to follow.

sentences.zh: 控馬者皆泣下。

translations.literal: Those holding the horses all wept.
translations.idiomatic: The men holding the horses wept as they watched.

sentences.zh: 諸將不得已與俱。

translations.literal: The generals, having no choice, went with him.
translations.idiomatic: The other generals had no choice but to go with him.

sentences.zh: 俄而敵大至，圍之數重。

translations.literal: Before long the enemy arrived in great force and surrounded them in many rings.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the enemy came in overwhelming numbers and surrounded them layer upon layer.

sentences.zh: 聰戰死，福及諸將皆被執遇害，年六十七，一軍皆沒。

translations.literal: Cong died in battle; Fu and the other generals were all captured and killed; he was sixty-seven years old, and the whole army was wiped out.
translations.idiomatic: Cong was killed in battle; Fu and the other generals were captured and put to death. Fu was sixty-seven. The entire army was annihilated.

sentences.zh: 敗聞，帝震怒。

translations.literal: When news of the defeat arrived, the emperor was shaken with rage.
translations.idiomatic: When word of the disaster reached the court, the emperor was furious.

sentences.zh: 以諸將無足任者，決計親征。

translations.literal: Because none of the generals were fit to be entrusted [with the task], he resolved to campaign in person.
translations.idiomatic: Concluding that no general was equal to the task, he decided to lead the campaign himself.

sentences.zh: 奪福世爵，徙其家海南。

translations.literal: Fu's hereditary title was stripped, and his family was banished to Hainan.
translations.idiomatic: Fu's hereditary title was revoked and his family was exiled to Hainan.

sentences.zh: 李遠 王忠 王聰 火真

translations.literal: Li Yuan, Wang Zhong, Wang Cong, Huo Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuan, Wang Zhong, Wang Cong, and Huo Zhen

sentences.zh: 李遠，懷遠人。

translations.literal: Li Yuan was a man of Huaiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuan was a native of Huaiyuan.

sentences.zh: 襲父職為蔚州衛指揮僉事。

translations.literal: He inherited his father's post as assistant commander of the Weizhou Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited his father's post as assistant commander of the Weizhou Guard.

sentences.zh: 燕兵攻蔚州，舉城降。

translations.literal: When the Yan army attacked Weizhou, the whole city surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Yan's army attacked Weizhou, the city surrendered en masse.

sentences.zh: 南軍駐德州，運道出徐、沛間。

translations.literal: The southern army was stationed at Dezhou, and the supply route ran through the region between Xu and Pei.
translations.idiomatic: The southern army was encamped at Dezhou, and its supply line ran through the Xu and Pei region.

sentences.zh: 遠以輕兵六千，詐為南軍袍鎧，人插柳一枝於背，徑濟寧、沙河至沛，無覺者。

translations.literal: Yuan with six thousand light troops, disguised in the robes and armor of the southern army, each man inserting one willow branch on his back, went straight through Jining and Shahe to Pei, and no one detected them.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan led six thousand light troops disguised in southern army armor, each man with a willow sprig thrust through the back of his collar, and marched straight through Jining and Shahe to Pei without being detected.

sentences.zh: 焚糧舟數萬，河水盡熱，魚鱉皆浮死。

translations.literal: They burned tens of thousands of grain boats; the river water grew hot throughout, and fish and turtles all floated up dead.
translations.idiomatic: They burned tens of thousands of grain barges; the river grew scalding hot, and fish and turtles floated up dead.

sentences.zh: 南將袁宇三萬騎來追，伏兵擊敗之。

translations.literal: The southern general Yuan Yu came in pursuit with thirty thousand horsemen; ambush troops struck and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: The southern general Yuan Yu pursued with thirty thousand cavalry, but Yuan's ambush routed him.

sentences.zh: 建文四年正月，燕軍駐蠡縣。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year of Jianwen, the Yan army was stationed at Li County.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourth year of the Jianwen reign, the Yan army was encamped at Li County.

sentences.zh: 遠分哨至槁城，遇德州將葛進步騎萬余，乘冰渡滹沱河。

translations.literal: Yuan sent out scouts as far as Gaocheng and encountered the Dezhou general Ge Jin with more than ten thousand infantry and cavalry, crossing the Hutuo River on the ice.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan sent out scouts toward Gaocheng and encountered the Dezhou general Ge Jin with more than ten thousand foot and horse soldiers crossing the frozen Hutuo River.

sentences.zh: 遠迎擊之。

translations.literal: Yuan went forward to meet and attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan rode out to meet and attack him.

sentences.zh: 進系馬林間，以步兵接戰。

translations.literal: Jin tied his horses in the forest and engaged with infantry.
translations.idiomatic: Jin tethered his horses in the woods and fought with infantry.

sentences.zh: 遠佯卻，潛分兵出其後，解所系馬，再戰。

translations.literal: Yuan feigned retreat, secretly divided troops to emerge behind them, untied the horses that had been tethered, and fought again.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan feigned retreat, then secretly sent men around behind the enemy, cut loose their tethered horses, and attacked again.

sentences.zh: 進引退失馬，遂大敗。

translations.literal: Jin drew back in retreat and lost his horses, and so suffered a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Jin fell back without his horses and was routed.

sentences.zh: 斬首四千，獲馬千匹。

translations.literal: Four thousand heads were cut off, and one thousand horses were captured.
translations.idiomatic: Four thousand heads were taken and a thousand horses captured.

sentences.zh: 成祖以歲首大捷，賜書嘉勞曰：「將軍以輕騎八百，破敵數萬，出奇應變，雖古名將不過也。

translations.literal: The Prince of Yan, because of the great victory at the year's opening, granted a letter of commendation and praise, saying: "General, with eight hundred light horsemen you broke tens of thousands of the enemy; deploying surprise and adapting to change — even the famed generals of antiquity could do no more.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Yan, delighted by this opening victory of the year, sent a letter of commendation: "With eight hundred light cavalry you routed an enemy tens of thousands strong — striking by surprise and adapting to circumstance. Even the greatest generals of antiquity could have done no better.

sentences.zh: 」復遣哨淮上，敗守淮將士，斬千余級。

translations.literal: " He again sent scouts onto the Huai, defeated the officers and soldiers defending the Huai, and cut off more than a thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: " He then sent scouts along the Huai, defeated the garrison there, and took more than a thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 累功為都督僉事，封安平侯，祿千石，予世伯券。

translations.literal: Through accumulated merit he became assistant regional commander, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Anping with an income of one thousand shi, and was granted a hereditary patent of nobility.
translations.idiomatic: For accumulated merit he was made assistant regional commander, enfeoffed as Marquis of Anping with an income of one thousand shi, and granted a hereditary patent of nobility.

sentences.zh: 永樂元年，偕武安侯鄭亨備宣府。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongle, together with the Marquis of Wu'an Zheng Heng he garrisoned Xuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Yongle reign, he joined the Marquis of Wu'an, Zheng Heng, in garrisoning Xuanfu.

sentences.zh: 遠沈毅有膽略，言論慷慨。

translations.literal: Yuan was deep and resolute, possessed of daring and strategy, and spoke with generous fervor.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan was resolute and bold, a man of daring and strategy who spoke with passionate conviction.

sentences.zh: 既從邱福出塞，至臚朐河。

translations.literal: Having followed Qiu Fu beyond the passes, he reached the Lulut River.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Qiu Fu beyond the frontier to the Lulut River.

sentences.zh: 諫福，不聽，師敗。

translations.literal: He remonstrated with Fu; [Fu] would not listen, and the army was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: He remonstrated with Fu, but Fu would not listen, and the army was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 遠帥五百騎突陣，殺數百人，馬蹶被執，罵不絕口死。

translations.literal: Yuan led five hundred horsemen in a charge through the enemy lines, killed several hundred men, his horse stumbled and he was captured, and he died cursing without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan led five hundred cavalry in a charge through the enemy ranks and killed several hundred men before his horse stumbled and he was captured; he died cursing without pause.

sentences.zh: 年四十六。

translations.literal: He was forty-six years old.
translations.idiomatic: He was forty-six.

sentences.zh: 追封莒國公，謚忠壯。

translations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Ju, with the posthumous title Zhongzhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Ju, with the posthumous name Loyal and Valiant.

sentences.zh: 子安，嗣伯爵。

translations.literal: His son An succeeded to the earldom.
translations.idiomatic: His son An inherited the earldom.

sentences.zh: 洪熙元年為交阯參將，失律，謫為事官。

translations.literal: In the first year of Hongxi he served as deputy commander in Jiaozhi; he violated military discipline and was demoted to officer-on-punishment duty.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Hongxi reign he served as deputy commander in Jiaozhi; after a breach of discipline he was demoted to penal service.

sentences.zh: 已，從王通棄交阯還，下獄奪券，謫赤城，立功。

translations.literal: Later, following Wang Tong in abandoning Jiaozhi and returning, he was imprisoned and stripped of his patent, banished to Chicheng, and [there] achieved merit.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when he withdrew from Jiaozhi with Wang Tong, he was imprisoned, stripped of his patent, and exiled to Chicheng, where he earned merit in service.

sentences.zh: 英宗即位，起都督僉事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yingzong acceded, he was restored as assistant regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yingzong came to the throne, he was restored to the rank of assistant regional commander.

sentences.zh: 征阿臺朵兒只伯。

translations.literal: He campaigned against Atai Duo'erzhibo.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in the campaign against Atai Duo'erzhibo.

sentences.zh: 遷都督同知，充總兵官，鎮松潘。

translations.literal: He was transferred to vice regional commander, appointed overall commander, and garrisoned Songpan.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice regional commander, appointed supreme commander, and stationed at Songpan.

sentences.zh: 正統六年，副定西伯蔣貴征麓川。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhengtong, as deputy to the Earl of Dingxi Jiang Gui he campaigned against Luchuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of the Zhengtong reign he served under the Earl of Dingxi, Jiang Gui, in the Luchuan campaign.

sentences.zh: 貴令安駐軍潞江護餉，而自帥大軍進。

translations.literal: Gui ordered An to encamp at Lujiang to guard the supplies, while he himself led the great army forward.
translations.idiomatic: Gui ordered An to hold Lujiang and guard the supply line while he led the main army forward.

sentences.zh: 賊破。

translations.literal: The bandits were broken.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels were defeated.

sentences.zh: 安恥無功，聞有餘賊屯高黎貢山，徑往擊之。

translations.literal: An was ashamed of having no achievement; hearing that remnant bandits were encamped on Gaoligong Mountain, he went straight to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed of having won no glory, An heard that remnant rebels were encamped on Gaoligong Mountain and marched straight against them.

sentences.zh: 為所敗，失士卒千餘人，都指揮趙斌等皆死。

translations.literal: He was defeated by them, lost more than a thousand officers and soldiers, and the regional commander Zhao Bin and others all died.
translations.idiomatic: He was defeated, losing more than a thousand men; the regional commander Zhao Bin and others were killed.

sentences.zh: 逮下獄，謫戍獨石。

translations.literal: He was arrested and imprisoned, and banished to garrison service at Dushi.
translations.idiomatic: He was arrested, imprisoned, and exiled to garrison duty at Dushi.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died there.

sentences.zh: 詔授子清都指揮同知。

translations.literal: An edict appointed his son Qing vice regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: By imperial edict his son Qing was appointed vice regional commander.

sentences.zh: 王忠，孝感人。

translations.literal: Wang Zhong was a man of Xiaogan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhong was a native of Xiaogan.

sentences.zh: 與李遠同降於蔚州。

translations.literal: Together with Li Yuan he surrendered at Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He surrendered at Weizhou together with Li Yuan.

sentences.zh: 每戰，帥精騎為奇兵，多斬獲。

translations.literal: In every battle he led elite horsemen as surprise troops and often achieved many kills and captures.
translations.idiomatic: In every battle he led elite cavalry as a flanking force and won many kills and captures.

sentences.zh: 累遷都督僉事，封靖安侯，祿千石。

translations.literal: Through successive promotions he became assistant regional commander, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Jing'an, with an income of one thousand shi.
translations.idiomatic: For accumulated merit he rose to assistant regional commander and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Jing'an with an income of one thousand shi.

sentences.zh: 出塞戰歿，年五十一，爵除。

translations.literal: He went beyond the passes, died in battle, was fifty-one years old, and his title was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: He died in battle beyond the frontier at the age of fifty-one, and his title was revoked.

sentences.zh: 王聰，蘄水人。

translations.literal: Wang Cong was a man of Qishui.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Cong was a native of Qishui.

sentences.zh: 以燕山中護衛百戶從起兵。

translations.literal: As a centurion of the Yan Mountain Central Guard he followed in raising the army.
translations.idiomatic: As a centurion of the Yan Mountain Central Guard he joined the prince's uprising.

sentences.zh: 取薊州，攻遵化，徇涿州。

translations.literal: He took Jizhou, attacked Zunhua, and swept through Zhuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He captured Jizhou, assaulted Zunhua, and swept through Zhuozhou.

sentences.zh: 轉戰茌平、滑口，破南軍，獲馬千五百。

translations.literal: He fought at Chiping and Huakou, broke the southern army, and captured one thousand five hundred horses.
translations.idiomatic: He fought at Chiping and Huakou, routed the southern army, and captured fifteen hundred horses.

sentences.zh: 還守保定。

translations.literal: He returned to garrison Baoding.
translations.idiomatic: He then returned to hold Baoding.

sentences.zh: 從次江上，略南軍舟濟師。

translations.literal: He followed in descending to the river, raided the southern army's boats, and ferried troops across.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the prince down to the Yangtze, seized southern boats, and ferried the army across.

sentences.zh: 累遷都指揮使。

translations.literal: Through accumulated promotions he became regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: For accumulated merit he rose to regional commander.

sentences.zh: 封武城侯，祿千五百石。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Marquis of Wucheng with an income of one thousand five hundred shi.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Marquis of Wucheng with an income of fifteen hundred shi.

sentences.zh: 偕同安侯火真備禦宣府。

translations.literal: Together with the Marquis of Tong'an Huo Zhen he prepared the defense of Xuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: Together with the Marquis of Tong'an, Huo Zhen, he garrisoned Xuanfu.

sentences.zh: 屢奉詔巡邊。

translations.literal: He repeatedly received edicts to patrol the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly ordered to patrol the frontier.

sentences.zh: 從邱福出塞，戰死，年五十三。

translations.literal: He followed Qiu Fu beyond the passes, died in battle, and was fifty-three years old.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Qiu Fu beyond the frontier and was killed in battle at the age of fifty-three.

sentences.zh: 追封漳國公，謚武毅。

translations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Zhang, with the posthumous title Wuyi.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Zhang, with the posthumous name Martial and Resolute.

sentences.zh: 子琰嗣。

translations.literal: His son Yan succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yan succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 聰及遠嘗諫福，故得褒恤。

translations.literal: Because Cong and Yuan had once remonstrated with Fu, they therefore received commendation and posthumous honors.
translations.idiomatic: Because Cong and Yuan had remonstrated with Fu, they received posthumous honors.

sentences.zh: 火真，蒙古人，初名火裏火真。

translations.literal: Huo Zhen was a Mongol; his original name was Huolihuo Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Huo Zhen was a Mongol whose original name was Huolihuo Zhen.

sentences.zh: 洪武時歸附，為燕山中護衛千戶。

translations.literal: During the Hongwu reign he submitted and was attached [to the Ming], serving as chiliarch of the Yan Mountain Central Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted to the Ming during the Hongwu reign and became a chiliarch of the Yan Mountain Central Guard.

sentences.zh: 從攻真定，先馳突耿炳文陣，大軍乘之，遂捷。

translations.literal: He followed in attacking Zhending, first galloping ahead to charge into Geng Bingwen's formation; the great army took advantage and thereupon achieved victory.
translations.idiomatic: At the attack on Zhending he galloped ahead and broke into Geng Bingwen's lines; the main army pressed the advantage and won.

sentences.zh: 從襲大寧，戰鄭村壩。

translations.literal: He followed in the surprise attack on Da Ning and fought at Zheng Village Dam.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in the surprise attack on Da Ning and fought at Zheng Village Dam.

sentences.zh: 日暝，天甚寒，真斂敝鞍爇火成祖前。

translations.literal: The sun set; the sky was very cold; Zhen gathered worn saddles and kindled a fire before the Prince of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk, in bitter cold, Zhen gathered worn saddles and built a fire before the prince.

sentences.zh: 甲士數人趨附火，衛士止之。

translations.literal: Several armored soldiers hurried to draw near the fire; the guards stopped them.
translations.idiomatic: Several armored soldiers pressed toward the fire, but the guards held them back.

sentences.zh: 成祖曰：「吾衣重裘猶寒。

translations.literal: The Prince of Yan said: "Even though I wear heavy furs I am still cold.
translations.idiomatic: The prince said, "Even wrapped in heavy furs I am cold.

sentences.zh: 此皆壯士，勿止也。

translations.literal: These are all brave warriors — do not stop them.
translations.idiomatic: These are brave men — let them come.

sentences.zh: 」聞者感泣。

translations.literal: " Those who heard were moved to tears.
translations.idiomatic: " Those who heard wept with gratitude.

sentences.zh: 真嘗將騎兵，每戰輒有斬獲，呼噪歸營，眾服其勇。

translations.literal: Zhen often commanded cavalry; in every battle he always had kills and captures, shouting and clamoring as he returned to camp, and the masses admired his bravery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen often led cavalry; in every battle he won kills and captures, returning to camp with shouts of triumph, and all admired his courage.

sentences.zh: 累遷都督僉事，封同安侯，祿千五石。

translations.literal: Through accumulated promotions he became assistant regional commander, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Tong'an, with an income of one thousand five hundred shi.
translations.idiomatic: For accumulated merit he rose to assistant regional commander and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Tong'an with an income of fifteen hundred shi.

sentences.zh: 出塞戰歿，年六十一。

translations.literal: He went beyond the passes, died in battle, and was sixty-one years old.
translations.idiomatic: He died in battle beyond the frontier at the age of sixty-one.

sentences.zh: 爵除。

translations.literal: His title was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: His title was revoked.

sentences.zh: 子孫世襲觀海衛千戶。

translations.literal: His descendants hereditarily inherited the post of chiliarch of the Guanhai Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His descendants inherited in perpetuity the post of chiliarch of the Guanhai Guard.

sentences.zh: 裔孫斌，嘉靖中武舉。

translations.literal: A descendant several generations removed, Bin, passed the military examination in the Jiajing reign.
translations.idiomatic: A distant descendant, Bin, passed the military examination during the Jiajing reign.

sentences.zh: 倭寇浙東，帥海舟與賊戰。

translations.literal: When Japanese pirates raided eastern Zhejiang, he led sea vessels to fight the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: When Japanese pirates raided eastern Zhejiang, he led a fleet against them.

sentences.zh: 賊然火球擲斌舟，斌輒手接之，還燒賊舟。

translations.literal: The bandits lit fire-balls and threw them at Bin's boat; Bin would catch them by hand and hurl them back to burn the bandits' boats.
translations.idiomatic: The pirates threw burning fireballs at Bin's vessel; he caught them bare-handed and hurled them back to set their ships ablaze.

sentences.zh: 賊屯補陀山，斌直搗其營，多殺傷。

translations.literal: The bandits were encamped on Putuo Mountain; Bin went straight to smash their camp and killed and wounded many.
translations.idiomatic: When the pirates encamped on Putuo Mountain, Bin attacked their camp directly and killed or wounded many.

sentences.zh: 後軍不繼，被擒。

translations.literal: The rear army did not follow up, and he was captured.
translations.idiomatic: When the rear guard failed to come up, he was captured.

sentences.zh: 不屈，賊支解之。

translations.literal: He would not submit, and the bandits dismembered him.
translations.idiomatic: He refused to submit, and the pirates dismembered him.

sentences.zh: 官為建祠曰「忠勇」。

translations.literal: The government built a shrine for him called "Loyal and Brave."
translations.idiomatic: The government built a shrine in his honor named Loyal and Brave.

sentences.zh: 譚淵，清流人。

translations.literal: Tan Yuan was a man of Qingliu.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Yuan was a native of Qingliu.

sentences.zh: 嗣父職為燕山右護衛副千戶。

translations.literal: He inherited his father's post as deputy chiliarch of the Yan Mountain Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited his father's post as deputy chiliarch of the Yan Mountain Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 燕兵起，從奪九門。

translations.literal: When the Yan army rose, he followed in seizing the Nine Gates.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince's army rose, he took part in seizing the Nine Gates of Beijing.

sentences.zh: 破雄縣。

translations.literal: He broke Xiong County.
translations.idiomatic: He captured Xiong County.

sentences.zh: 潘忠、楊松自鄚州來援，淵帥壯士千餘人，伏月漾橋水中，人持茭草一束，蒙頭通鼻息。

translations.literal: Pan Zhong and Yang Song came from Mozhou to reinforce; Yuan led more than a thousand stalwart men, lying in ambush in the water at Yueyang Bridge, each man holding one bundle of rush grass, covering the head to breathe through the nose.
translations.idiomatic: When Pan Zhong and Yang Song marched from Mozhou to relieve the city, Yuan led more than a thousand picked men in ambush beneath the waters of Yueyang Bridge, each holding a bundle of rushes over his head to breathe through.

sentences.zh: 南軍已過，即出據橋。

translations.literal: After the southern army had passed, they immediately emerged and seized the bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Once the southern army had passed, they rose from the water and seized the bridge.

sentences.zh: 忠等戰敗，趨橋不得渡，遂被擒。

translations.literal: Zhong and the others were defeated in battle; rushing to the bridge they could not cross, and so were captured.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong and his men were defeated; racing for the bridge they found it held and were captured.

sentences.zh: 累進都指揮同知。

translations.literal: Through accumulated promotions he advanced to vice regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: For accumulated merit he rose to vice regional commander.

sentences.zh: 淵驍勇善戰，引兩石弓，射無不中。

translations.literal: Yuan was fierce and brave and skilled in battle; he drew a two-stone bow, and in shooting nothing missed.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan was a fierce and capable fighter who could draw a two-stone bow and never missed his mark.

sentences.zh: 然性嗜殺。

translations.literal: Yet by nature he was addicted to killing.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he had a bloodthirsty nature.

sentences.zh: 滄州破，成祖命給牒散降卒。

translations.literal: When Cangzhou fell, Chen Zu ordered that certificates be issued and the surrendered soldiers be dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: After Cangzhou fell, Chen Zu ordered certificates issued and the surrendered troops sent home.

sentences.zh: 未遣者三千餘人，待明給牒。

translations.literal: More than three thousand who had not yet been sent off were waiting until dawn for their certificates.
translations.idiomatic: More than three thousand who had not yet been released were waiting until morning for their papers.

sentences.zh: 淵一夜盡殺之。

translations.literal: In one night Yuan killed them all.
translations.idiomatic: In a single night Yuan slaughtered them all.

sentences.zh: 王怒。

translations.literal: The prince was angry.
translations.idiomatic: The prince was furious.

sentences.zh: 淵曰：「此曹皆壯士，釋之為後患。

translations.literal: Yuan said, "These men are all stalwart warriors; if released they will become a later calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan said, "These are all fighting men; if we let them go they will be trouble later.

sentences.zh: 」王曰：「如爾言，當盡殺敵。

translations.literal: " The prince said, "By your reasoning, one ought to kill all the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: " The prince replied, "By that logic you ought to kill every enemy.

sentences.zh: 敵可盡乎？

translations.literal: Can the enemy be exhausted?
translations.idiomatic: Can you ever kill them all?

sentences.zh: 」淵慚而退。

translations.literal: " Yuan, ashamed, withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: " Yuan withdrew in shame.

sentences.zh: 夾河之戰，南軍陣動塵起。

translations.literal: At the Battle of Jiahe, the southern army's formation stirred and dust rose.
translations.idiomatic: At the Battle of Jiahe, the southern army's lines shifted and dust billowed up.

sentences.zh: 淵遽前搏戰，馬蹶被殺。

translations.literal: Yuan hurried forward to grapple in battle; his horse stumbled and he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan charged forward to fight hand to hand; his horse stumbled and he was killed.

sentences.zh: 成祖悼惜之。

translations.literal: Chen Zu mourned and regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zu mourned his loss deeply.

sentences.zh: 即位，贈都指揮使，追封崇安侯，謚壯節，立祠祀之。

translations.literal: Upon taking the throne, he was posthumously granted regional commander, posthumously enfeoffed as Marquis of Chong'an, given the posthumous title Zhuangjie, and a shrine was established to sacrifice to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Zu took the throne, he posthumously made Yuan regional commander, enfeoffed him as Marquis of Chong'an with the posthumous name Zhuangjie, and had a shrine built in his honor.

sentences.zh: 子忠，從入京師有功。

translations.literal: His son Zhong followed in entering the capital and had merit.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhong distinguished himself in the march on the capital.

sentences.zh: 又以淵故封新寧伯，祿千石。

translations.literal: Also because of Yuan he was enfeoffed as Earl of Xinning, with an emolument of one thousand shi.
translations.idiomatic: In recognition of Yuan's service he was enfeoffed as Earl of Xinning with an income of one thousand shi.

sentences.zh: 永樂二十一年，將右哨從征沙漠。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year of Yongle, he commanded the right vanguard in the desert campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year of Yongle he led the right vanguard on the desert campaign.

sentences.zh: 宣德元年從征樂安。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xuande he followed the campaign against Le'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xuande he took part in the campaign against Le'an.

sentences.zh: 三年坐征交阯失律，下獄論死，已得釋，卒。

translations.literal: In the third year, on account of misconduct in the Jiaozhi campaign, he was imprisoned and sentenced to death; he was already released when he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was imprisoned and sentenced to death for misconduct during the Jiaozhi campaign; he was released before he died.

sentences.zh: 子璟乞嗣。

translations.literal: His son Jing requested to inherit.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jing petitioned to inherit the title.

sentences.zh: 吏部言忠罪死，不當襲。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Personnel said Zhong had been condemned to death for a crime and ought not inherit.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Personnel argued that because Zhong had been sentenced to death, the title should not pass down.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「券有免死文，其予嗣。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "The warrant contains text exempting from death; let him inherit.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "The warrant of mercy contains a clause sparing his life; let the succession go to his heir.

sentences.zh: 」再傳至孫祐。

translations.literal: " After two more generations it passed to the grandson You.
translations.idiomatic: " The title passed through two more generations to his grandson You.

sentences.zh: 成化中，協守南京。

translations.literal: During the Chenghua reign he jointly defended Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chenghua reign he served as co-garrison commander of Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 還，掌前府提督團營，累加太傅，嗣伯，六十九年始卒。

translations.literal: Returning, he took charge of the Front Guard and supervised the regiment camps, was repeatedly promoted to Grand Tutor, inherited the earldom, and only died in his sixty-ninth year.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he took command of the Front Guard and supervised the regiment camps, rose to Grand Tutor, inherited the earldom, and lived to sixty-nine before he died.

sentences.zh: 謚莊僖。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Zhuangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously named Zhuangxi.

sentences.zh: 子綸嗣。

translations.literal: His son Lun inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Lun succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十四年鎮湖廣，剿九溪蠻有功，益祿。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Jiajing he garrisoned Huguang, suppressed the Jiuxi barbarians with merit, and received increased emolument.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Jiajing he was posted to Huguang, where he distinguished himself suppressing the Jiuxi tribes and received an increase in stipend.

sentences.zh: 坐占役軍士奪爵。

translations.literal: On account of illegally employing soldiers he was stripped of his title.
translations.idiomatic: He was stripped of his title for illegally impressing soldiers for private use.

sentences.zh: 數傳至弘業，國亡，死於賊。

translations.literal: After several generations it passed to Hongye; when the dynasty fell, he died at the hands of bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The line passed through several generations to Hongye, who was killed by rebels when the dynasty fell.

sentences.zh: 真勇健有智略。

translations.literal: Zhen was brave, robust, and possessed of strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen was brave, hardy, and resourceful.

sentences.zh: 成祖每追悼之曰：「奮武如王真，何功不成！

translations.literal: Chen Zu, whenever he mourned him, would say, "With martial ardor like Wang Zhen's, what achievement could fail!
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zu often mourned him, saying, "A man who fights like Wang Zhen—what could he not accomplish!

sentences.zh: 不死，功當冠諸將。

translations.literal: Had he not died, his achievements would have topped all the generals.
translations.idiomatic: Had he lived, his achievements would have surpassed every other general.

sentences.zh: 」仁宗時，追封寧國公，加號效忠。

translations.literal: " In the time of Emperor Renzong he was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Ningguo, with the added honorific Xiaozhong.
translations.idiomatic: " Under Emperor Renzong he was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Ningguo with the honorific title Xiaozhong.

sentences.zh: 子通自有傳。

translations.literal: His son Tong has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Tong has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 燕師起，亨與劉真、卜萬守大寧。

translations.literal: When the Yan army rose, Heng together with Liu Zhen and Bu Wan defended Daning.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince's army rose, Heng, Liu Zhen, and Bu Wan held Daning.

sentences.zh: 移兵出松亭關，駐沙河，謀攻遵化。

translations.literal: They moved troops out through Songting Pass, encamped at Shahe, and planned to attack Zunhua.
translations.idiomatic: They marched out through Songting Pass, encamped at Shahe, and planned an attack on Zunhua.

sentences.zh: 燕兵至，退保關。

translations.literal: When the Yan army arrived, they withdrew to hold the pass.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince's army arrived, they fell back to defend the pass.

sentences.zh: 當是時，李景隆帥五十萬眾將攻北平。

translations.literal: At that time Li Jinglong commanded five hundred thousand troops and was about to attack Beiping.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Li Jinglong was leading five hundred thousand men in an advance on Beiping.

sentences.zh: 北平勢弱，而大寧行都司所領興州、營州二十余衛，皆西北精銳；

translations.literal: Beiping's position was weak, yet the more than twenty guards of Xingzhou and Yingzhou under the Daning Regional Military Commission were all elite troops of the northwest;
translations.idiomatic: Beiping was dangerously weak, yet the more than twenty guards of Xingzhou and Yingzhou under the Daning Regional Military Commission were the finest troops of the northwest;

sentences.zh: 朵顏、泰寧、福余三衛，元降將所統番騎廣卒，尤驍勇。

translations.literal: the three guards of Doyin, Taining, and Fuyu, barbarian cavalry and broad soldiery commanded by Yuan surrender generals, were especially fierce and brave.
translations.idiomatic: and the three guards of Doyin, Taining, and Fuyu—barbarian cavalry under Yuan surrender generals—were especially fierce.

sentences.zh: 卜萬將與景隆軍合。

translations.literal: Bu Wan was about to join forces with Jinglong's army.
translations.idiomatic: Bu Wan was on the verge of linking up with Jinglong's army.

sentences.zh: 成祖懼，以計紿亨囚萬，遂從劉家口間道疾攻大寧。

translations.literal: Chen Zu was afraid; by stratagem he deceived Heng and imprisoned Wan, then by a secret route through Liujiakou swiftly attacked Daning.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zu, alarmed, tricked Heng into helping him imprison Wan, then struck Daning by a secret route through Liujiakou.

sentences.zh: 亨及劉真自松亭回救，中道聞大寧破，乃與指揮徐理、陳文等謀降燕。

translations.literal: Heng and Liu Zhen returned from Songting to relieve the city; midway they heard Daning had fallen, and so with the commanders Xu Li, Chen Wen, and others plotted to surrender to Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Heng and Liu Zhen marched back from Songting to relieve the city, but halfway there learned that Daning had fallen; they then conspired with the commanders Xu Li, Chen Wen, and others to defect to the prince.

sentences.zh: 夜二鼓，襲劉真營。

translations.literal: At the second watch of the night they attacked Liu Zhen's camp.
translations.idiomatic: At the second watch of the night they raided Liu Zhen's camp.

sentences.zh: 真單騎走廣寧，亨等帥眾降。

translations.literal: Zhen fled alone on horseback to Guangning; Heng and the others led the troops in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen fled alone on horseback to Guangning while Heng and the others brought their men over in surrender.

sentences.zh: 成祖盡拔諸軍及三衛騎卒，挾寧王以歸。

translations.literal: Chen Zu drew off all the armies and the cavalry of the three guards, taking the Prince of Ning with him on the return.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zu marched off with every unit and the cavalry of the three guards, bringing the Prince of Ning with him.

sentences.zh: 自是沖鋒陷陣多三衛兵。

translations.literal: From then on, in charging the vanguard and breaking enemy lines, it was mostly soldiers of the three guards.
translations.idiomatic: From then on his shock troops in the van were largely drawn from the three guards.

sentences.zh: 成祖取天下，自克大寧始。

translations.literal: Chen Zu's winning of the empire began with the capture of Daning.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zu's path to the throne began with the capture of Daning.

sentences.zh: 亨、理既降，累從破南軍。

translations.literal: After Heng and Li had surrendered, they repeatedly followed in defeating the southern army.
translations.idiomatic: Once Heng and Xu Li had defected, they fought repeatedly and helped break the southern armies.

sentences.zh: 白溝河之戰，亨中創幾死。

translations.literal: At the Battle of Baigou River, Heng was wounded in battle and nearly died.
translations.idiomatic: At the Battle of Baigou River Heng was badly wounded and nearly killed.

sentences.zh: 已，攻濟南，與平安戰鏵山，大敗。

translations.literal: Later, attacking Jinan, he fought Ping An at Huashan and was utterly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Later, during the assault on Jinan, he fought Ping An at Huashan and suffered a crushing defeat.

sentences.zh: 創甚，輿還北平。

translations.literal: His wounds were severe; he was carried back to Beiping in a litter.
translations.idiomatic: Badly wounded, he was carried back to Beiping in a litter.

sentences.zh: 進都督同知。

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice regional commander.

sentences.zh: 成祖還軍，親詣亨第勞問。

translations.literal: When Chen Zu returned the army, he personally went to Heng's residence to console and inquire.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Zu returned with the army, he went in person to Heng's home to comfort him.

sentences.zh: 其年十月卒。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of that year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died that October.

sentences.zh: 成祖自為文以祭。

translations.literal: Chen Zu himself composed a text to sacrifice to him.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zu wrote the funeral elegy and offered sacrifice himself.

sentences.zh: 比即位，追封涇國公，謚襄敏。

translations.literal: By the time he took the throne, he was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Jing, with the posthumous title Xiangmin.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Zu took the throne, he posthumously enfeoffed Heng as Duke of Jing with the posthumous name Xiangmin.

sentences.zh: 長子恭，嗣都督同知。

translations.literal: The eldest son Gong inherited the post of vice regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Gong inherited the post of vice regional commander.

sentences.zh: 子 懋

translations.literal: Son: Mao
translations.idiomatic: Son: Mao

sentences.zh: 少子懋，初以舍人從軍，立功為指揮僉事。

translations.literal: The younger son Mao, at first as a household attendant followed the army, achieved merit and became assistant commander.
translations.idiomatic: The younger son Mao first entered service as a household attendant with the army; for his achievements he was made assistant commander.

sentences.zh: 已而將亨兵，功多，累進右都督。

translations.literal: Later he commanded Heng's troops; his achievements were many, and through repeated promotions he advanced to right regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: He later took command of Heng's troops, won many victories, and rose to right regional commander.

sentences.zh: 永樂元年，封寧陽伯，祿千石。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongle he was enfeoffed as Earl of Ningyang, with an emolument of one thousand shi.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongle he was enfeoffed as Earl of Ningyang with an income of one thousand shi.

sentences.zh: 六年三月佩征西將軍印，鎮寧夏，善撫降卒。

translations.literal: In the third month of the sixth year he wore the seal of General Who Pacifies the West, garrisoned Ningxia, and was skilled at comforting surrendered soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the sixth year he was invested with the seal of General Who Pacifies the West and posted to Ningxia, where he treated surrendered troops with great care.

sentences.zh: 明年秋，故元丞相昝卜及平章、司徒、國公、知院十余人，皆帥眾相繼來降。

translations.literal: The next autumn, the former Yuan chancellor Zan Bu and more than ten others—vice chancellors, ministers of education, dukes, and directors—each leading troops came in succession to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The following autumn more than ten former Yuan officials—including the chancellor Zan Bu, vice chancellors, ministers of education, dukes, and court directors—surrendered one after another with their followers.

sentences.zh: 已而平章都連等叛去，懋追擒之黑山，盡收所部人口畜牧。

translations.literal: Later the vice chancellor Du Lian and others rebelled and fled; Mao pursued and captured them at Heishan, fully recovering the people and livestock under their command.
translations.idiomatic: When the vice chancellor Du Lian and others later rebelled and fled, Mao pursued them to Heishan, captured them, and recovered all the people and livestock they had taken.

sentences.zh: 進侯，益祿二百石。

translations.literal: He was advanced to marquis, with emolument increased by two hundred shi.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to marquis and his stipend increased by two hundred shi.

sentences.zh: 八年從北征，督左掖。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he followed the northern campaign and supervised the left flank.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he joined the northern campaign as commander of the left flank.

sentences.zh: 十一年巡寧夏邊。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he inspected the Ningxia frontier.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he inspected the Ningxia border.

sentences.zh: 尋命將山西、陜西二都司及鞏昌、平涼諸衛兵，駐宣府。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered to command the troops of the two regional military commissions of Shanxi and Shaanxi and the guards of Gongchang, Pingliang, and others, garrisoning Xuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon ordered to take command of the Shanxi and Shaanxi regional armies and the guards of Gongchang, Pingliang, and elsewhere, and to garrison Xuanfu.

sentences.zh: 明年從北征，領左哨。

translations.literal: The next year he followed the northern campaign and led the left vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he joined the northern campaign in command of the left vanguard.

sentences.zh: 戰忽失溫，與成山侯王通先登，都督朱崇等乘之，遂大捷。

translations.literal: Fighting at Onon, together with Wang Tong, Marquis of Chengshan, he was first to ascend; regional commander Zhu Chong and others pressed the advantage, and so there was a great victory.
translations.idiomatic: At the battle of Onon he and Wang Tong, Marquis of Chengshan, were first over the enemy lines; Zhu Chong and the other commanders pressed the attack, and the victory was complete.

sentences.zh: 明年復鎮寧夏。

translations.literal: The next year he again garrisoned Ningxia.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he returned to garrison Ningxia.

sentences.zh: 二十年從北征。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he followed the northern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year he took part in the northern campaign.

sentences.zh: 領御前精騎破敵於屈裂河。

translations.literal: Leading the emperor's elite cavalry he defeated the enemy at the Qulie River.
translations.idiomatic: At the head of the emperor's picked cavalry he routed the enemy at the Qulie River.

sentences.zh: 別將五千騎循河東北，捕余寇，殲之山澤中。

translations.literal: Separately he led five thousand cavalry northeast along the river, hunted down the remaining bandits, and annihilated them in the mountains and marshes.
translations.idiomatic: He then led five thousand horsemen northeast along the river, ran down the remaining raiders, and wiped them out in the hills and marshes.

sentences.zh: 師還，武安侯鄭亨將輜重先行，懋伏隘以待。

translations.literal: When the army returned, Zheng Heng, Marquis of Wu'an, led the baggage train ahead; Mao lay in ambush at a defile to wait.
translations.idiomatic: On the return march Zheng Heng, Marquis of Wu'an, moved ahead with the baggage train while Mao lay in ambush at a pass.

sentences.zh: 敵來躡，伏起縱擊，敵死過半。

translations.literal: The enemy came in pursuit; the ambush rose and unleashed the attack, and more than half the enemy died.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy came in pursuit, his men sprang the ambush and cut them down; more than half were killed.

sentences.zh: 還京，賜龍衣玉帶，冊其女為麗妃。

translations.literal: Returning to the capital, he was granted dragon robes and a jade belt, and his daughter was ennobled as Consort Li.
translations.idiomatic: Back in the capital he was rewarded with dragon robes and a jade belt, and his daughter was made Consort Li.

sentences.zh: 明年將陜西、寧夏、甘肅三鎮兵，從征阿魯臺，為前鋒。

translations.literal: The next year he commanded the troops of the three garrisons of Shaanxi, Ningxia, and Gansu, followed the campaign against Aruqtai, and served as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he led the armies of the Shaanxi, Ningxia, and Gansu garrisons against Aruqtai as vanguard.

sentences.zh: 又明年復領前鋒，從北征。

translations.literal: Again the next year he once more led the vanguard in the northern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: The year after that he again led the vanguard on the northern campaign.

sentences.zh: 英宗即位，命偕張輔參議朝政，出為平羌將軍，鎮甘肅。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yingzong came to the throne, he was ordered together with Zhang Fu to deliberate on court affairs; then he went out as General Who Pacifies the Qiang and garrisoned Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yingzong ascended the throne, Mao was appointed to deliberate on state affairs with Zhang Fu, then sent out as General Who Pacifies the Qiang to garrison Gansu.

sentences.zh: 其冬，寇掠鎮番，懋遣兵援之，解去，以斬獲聞。

translations.literal: That winter, bandits raided Zhenfan; Mao sent troops to relieve it, they dispersed and withdrew, and he reported heads and captures.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, when raiders struck Zhenfan, Mao sent reinforcements, drove them off, and reported kills and captures.

sentences.zh: 參贊侍郎柴車劾懋失律致寇，又取所遺老弱，冒為都指揮馬亮等功受升賞，論斬。

translations.literal: Participating secretary Chai Che impeached Mao for misconduct that brought on the raid, and also for taking the old and weak left behind and falsely claiming them as the achievements of regional commander Ma Liang and others to receive promotion and reward; he was sentenced to decapitation.
translations.idiomatic: The participating secretary Chai Che impeached Mao for lax command that had invited the raid, and for seizing the old and weak the enemy had abandoned and passing them off as the kills of regional commander Ma Liang and others to win promotion and reward; he was sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 詔免死，奪祿。

translations.literal: An edict spared him from death and stripped his emolument.
translations.idiomatic: An edict spared his life but stripped his stipend.

sentences.zh: 久之還祿，奉朝請。

translations.literal: After a long time his emolument was restored, and he attended court audiences.
translations.idiomatic: After a time his stipend was restored and he resumed attendance at court.

sentences.zh: 十三年，福建賊鄧茂七反。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year the Fujian bandit Deng Maoqi rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year the Fujian rebel Deng Maoqi rose in revolt.

sentences.zh: 都御史張楷討之無功，乃詔懋佩征南將軍印，充總兵官，帥京營、江浙兵往討。

translations.literal: Censor-in-chief Zhang Kai campaigned against him without success, so Mao was ordered to wear the seal of General Who Pacifies the South, serve as overall commander, and lead the capital garrison and Jiangsu-Zhejiang troops to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: When the censor-in-chief Zhang Kai failed to suppress him, Mao was invested with the seal of General Who Pacifies the South, made overall commander, and sent with the capital garrison and Jiangsu-Zhejiang troops to crush the rebellion.

sentences.zh: 至浙江，有欲分兵扼海口者，懋曰：「是使賊致死於我也。

translations.literal: Reaching Zhejiang, there were those who wished to divide the army to block the river mouth; Mao said, "That would make the bandits fight to the death against us.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching Zhejiang, some officers proposed dividing the force to block the river mouth; Mao said, "That would only drive the rebels to fight us to the death.

sentences.zh: 」明年抵建寧，茂七已死，余賊聚尤溪、沙縣。

translations.literal: " The next year he reached Jianning; Maoqi was already dead, and the remaining bandits gathered at Youxi and Shaxian.
translations.idiomatic: " The following year he reached Jianning; Maoqi was already dead, and the remaining rebels had gathered at Youxi and Shaxian.

sentences.zh: 諸將欲屠之，懋曰：「是堅賊心也。

translations.literal: The generals wished to slaughter them; Mao said, "That would harden the bandits' hearts.
translations.idiomatic: When the generals proposed massacring them, Mao said, "That would only steel their resolve.

sentences.zh: 」乃下令招撫，賊黨多降。

translations.literal: " He then ordered offers of amnesty and pacification, and many of the bandit factions surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: " He ordered an offer of amnesty instead, and many rebels surrendered.

sentences.zh: 分道逐捕，悉平之。

translations.literal: Dividing forces to pursue and capture them, he entirely pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent columns in pursuit and brought the entire region under control.

sentences.zh: 已而沙縣賊復熾，久不定。

translations.literal: Later the bandits of Shaxian again flared up, and for a long time were not settled.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the rebels in Shaxian flared up again and remained unsettled for a long time.

sentences.zh: 會英宗北狩，景帝立，遂詔班師。

translations.literal: It happened that Emperor Yingzong went north on campaign and was captured; Emperor Jingdi came to the throne, and so an edict ordered withdrawal of the army.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Emperor Yingzong was captured on the northern frontier and Emperor Jingdi took the throne; an edict recalled the army.

sentences.zh: 言官劾之，以賊平不問。

translations.literal: Censorial officials impeached him, but because the bandits had been pacified he was not prosecuted.
translations.idiomatic: Censorial officials impeached him, but because the rebels had been suppressed he was not punished.

sentences.zh: 仍加太保，掌中府，兼領宗人府事。

translations.literal: He was still promoted to Grand Guardian, took charge of the Central Guard, and concurrently oversaw the affairs of the Imperial Clan Court.
translations.idiomatic: He was nonetheless promoted to Grand Guardian, placed in command of the Central Guard, and given concurrent charge of the Imperial Clan Court.

sentences.zh: 英宗復位，益祿二百石。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yingzong was restored to the throne, his emolument was increased by two hundred shi.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yingzong was restored to the throne, his stipend was increased by two hundred shi.

sentences.zh: 天順七年卒，年八十四。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Tianshun he died, aged eighty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the seventh year of Tianshun at the age of eighty-four.

sentences.zh: 贈浚國公，謚武靖。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Duke of Jun, with the posthumous title Wujing.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Jun with the posthumous name Wujing.

sentences.zh: 懋修髯偉貌，聲如洪鐘。

translations.literal: Mao had a long beard and a grand appearance; his voice was like a great bell.
translations.idiomatic: Mao wore a long beard and had a commanding presence; his voice rang like a great bell.

sentences.zh: 胸次磊落，敬禮士大夫。

translations.literal: His breast was open and magnanimous; he showed respect to scholar-officials.
translations.idiomatic: He was open-hearted and magnanimous and treated scholar-officials with respect.

sentences.zh: 「靖難」功臣至天順時無在者，惟懋久享祿位，數廢數起，卒以功名終。

translations.literal: Among the "Pacify Difficulties" merit lords, by the Tianshun period none remained; only Mao long enjoyed salary and rank, was several times dismissed and restored, and in the end finished with merit and fame.
translations.idiomatic: Of the Jingnan merit lords, none survived to the Tianshun reign; only Mao long enjoyed rank and stipend, was dismissed and restored several times, and ended his career with honor intact.

sentences.zh: 長子晟有罪，弟潤嗣。

translations.literal: The eldest son Sheng was guilty; the younger brother Run succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: The eldest son Sheng was convicted of a crime, and the younger brother Run succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 潤卒，弟瑛嗣，減祿之半，嗣侯。

translations.literal: When Run died, the younger brother Ying succeeded; the salary was halved, and he inherited the marquisate.
translations.idiomatic: When Run died, his younger brother Ying succeeded with half the stipend and inherited the marquisate.

sentences.zh: 十六年而晟子輔已長，乃令輔嗣，瑛免為勛衛。

translations.literal: After sixteen years Sheng's son Fu had grown up; he was then made to succeed, and Ying was excused to serve as an imperial guard.
translations.idiomatic: Sixteen years later, when Sheng's son Fu had come of age, Fu was restored to the succession and Ying was made an imperial guard instead.

sentences.zh: 輔後坐事失侯。

translations.literal: Fu later, because of an offense, lost the marquisate.
translations.idiomatic: Fu later lost the title for an offense.

sentences.zh: 卒，無子。

translations.literal: He died without sons.
translations.idiomatic: He died without an heir.

sentences.zh: 復封瑛孫繼祖為侯，傳爵至明亡。

translations.literal: Ying's grandson Jizu was again enfeoffed as marquis; the title passed down until the Ming perished.
translations.idiomatic: Ying's grandson Jizu was enfeoffed as marquis again, and the line continued until the fall of the Ming.

sentences.zh: 徐理 陳文 房寬 劉才

translations.literal: Xu Li, Chen Wen, Fang Kuan, Liu Cai.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Li, Chen Wen, Fang Kuan, and Liu Cai

sentences.zh: 徐理，西平人。

translations.literal: Xu Li was a man of Xiping.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Li was a native of Xiping.

sentences.zh: 洪武時，為永清中護衛指揮僉事，改營州衛。

translations.literal: In the Hongwu period he was assistant commander of the Yongqing Central Guard, then transferred to Yingzhou Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Under Hongwu he served as assistant commander of the Yongqing Central Guard and was later transferred to Yingzhou Guard.

sentences.zh: 既降，為右軍副將。

translations.literal: After he surrendered, he became deputy general of the Right Army.
translations.idiomatic: After he defected, he became deputy general of the Right Army.

sentences.zh: 每戰先登，有功。

translations.literal: In every battle he was first to ascend; he had merit.
translations.idiomatic: In every battle he was first over the wall and won distinction.

sentences.zh: 成祖將襲滄州，命理及陳旭潛於直沽造浮橋，以濟師。

translations.literal: When Chengzu was about to strike Cangzhou, he ordered Li and Chen Xu to build a pontoon bridge in secret at Zhigu to ferry the army across.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince planned to strike Cangzhou, he ordered Li and Chen Xu to build a pontoon bridge in secret at Zhigu to ferry the army across.

sentences.zh: 累進都指揮僉事，封武康伯。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to assistant regional commander and enfeoffed as Marquis of Wukang.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to assistant regional commander and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Wukang.

sentences.zh: 還守北平。

translations.literal: He returned to guard Beiping.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to garrison Beiping.

sentences.zh: 理馭下寬，得士卒心。

translations.literal: Li was lenient in governing subordinates and won the soldiers' hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Li ruled his men with leniency and won their loyalty.

sentences.zh: 永樂六年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the sixth year of Yongle.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixth year of Yongle.

sentences.zh: 再傳至孫勇，無子絕封。

translations.literal: After two generations it reached the grandson Yong; without sons the enfeoffment ended.
translations.idiomatic: The title passed to his grandson Yong, who died without heirs and the line ended.

sentences.zh: 陳文，降後為前軍左副將。

translations.literal: Chen Wen, after surrendering, became left deputy general of the Forward Army.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Wen, after defecting, became left deputy general of the Forward Army.

sentences.zh: 戰小河，死於陣。

translations.literal: Fighting at Xiaohe, he died on the battlefield.
translations.idiomatic: He was killed in battle at Xiaohe.

sentences.zh: 房寬，陳州人。

translations.literal: Fang Kuan was a man of Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Kuan was a native of Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 洪武中，以濟寧左衛指揮從徐達練兵北平，遂為北平都指揮同知，移守大寧。

translations.literal: In the Hongwu period, as commander of Jining Left Guard he followed Xu Da to drill troops at Beiping, then became vice regional commander of Beiping, and was transferred to guard Daning.
translations.idiomatic: Under Hongwu, as commander of Jining Left Guard he followed Xu Da to train troops at Beiping, became vice regional commander of Beiping, and was posted to guard Daning.

sentences.zh: 寬在邊久，凡山川塞，殊域情偽，莫不畢知，然不能撫士卒。

translations.literal: Kuan was long on the frontier; mountains, rivers, passes, and the truth and falsehood of foreign regions—none were not fully known to him; yet he could not comfort the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Kuan spent many years on the frontier and knew every pass and foreign land intimately, yet he could not win his soldiers' affection.

sentences.zh: 燕兵奄至，城中縛寬以降。

translations.literal: When the Yan army suddenly arrived, the city bound Kuan and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yan army appeared suddenly, the garrison bound Kuan and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 成祖釋之，俾領其眾。

translations.literal: Chengzu released him and had him lead his former troops.
translations.idiomatic: The prince released him and put him in command of his former troops.

sentences.zh: 戰白溝河，將右軍，失利。

translations.literal: Fighting at the White Ditch River, he commanded the Right Army and met with defeat.
translations.idiomatic: At the White Ditch River he commanded the Right Army and suffered a defeat.

sentences.zh: 從克廣昌、彰德，進都督僉事。

translations.literal: He followed in taking Guangchang and Zhangde and was promoted to assistant regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: He helped take Guangchang and Zhangde and was promoted to assistant regional commander.

sentences.zh: 以舊臣，略其過。

translations.literal: As an old minister, his faults were overlooked.
translations.idiomatic: As a veteran of long service, his faults were overlooked.

sentences.zh: 封思恩侯，祿八百石，世指揮使。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Marquis of Si'en, salary eight hundred shi, hereditary commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Marquis of Si'en with a stipend of eight hundred shi and a hereditary commander's rank.

sentences.zh: 永樂七年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the seventh year of Yongle.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the seventh year of Yongle.

sentences.zh: 劉才，字子才，霍丘人。

translations.literal: Liu Cai, styled Zicai, was a man of Huoqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cai, styled Zicai, was a native of Huoqiu.

sentences.zh: 元末為元帥，明興歸附，歷營州中護衛指揮僉事。

translations.literal: At the end of the Yuan he was a marshal; when the Ming rose he submitted, and served through as assistant commander of Yingzhou Central Guard.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Yuan he was a marshal; when the Ming rose he submitted and served as assistant commander of Yingzhou Central Guard.

sentences.zh: 燕師襲大寧，才降。

translations.literal: When the Yan army raided Daning, Cai surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yan army struck Daning, Cai surrendered.

sentences.zh: 從戰有功，封廣恩伯，祿九百石，世指揮同知。

translations.literal: He followed in battle with merit, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Guang'en, salary nine hundred shi, hereditary vice commander.
translations.idiomatic: He fought with distinction and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Guang'en with a stipend of nine hundred shi and a hereditary vice commander's rank.

sentences.zh: 永樂八年，從北征，督右掖。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Yongle he followed the northern campaign and supervised the right wing.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Yongle he joined the northern campaign as supervisor of the right wing.

sentences.zh: 失律議罪，既而宥之。

translations.literal: For breach of discipline he was judged guilty, but soon pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: He was found guilty of a disciplinary offense but was soon pardoned.

sentences.zh: 二十一年偕隆平侯張信理永平、山海邊務。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, together with the Marquis of Longping, Zhang Xin, he managed border affairs at Yongping and Shanhai.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year he and the Marquis of Longping, Zhang Xin, were put in charge of border affairs at Yongping and Shanhaiguan.

sentences.zh: 明年復從北征，至懷來，以疾還。

translations.literal: The next year he again followed the northern campaign; reaching Huailai, he returned because of illness.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he joined another northern campaign but turned back at Huailai because of illness.

sentences.zh: 才悃愊無華，不為茍合，亦不輕訾毀人，甚為仁宗所重。

translations.literal: Cai was sincere and without ornament, would not compromise improperly, and did not lightly slander others; he was greatly valued by Emperor Ren.
translations.idiomatic: Cai was plain and sincere, would not curry favor, and did not lightly speak ill of others; the Hongxi Emperor held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 宣德五年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the fifth year of Xuande.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifth year of Xuande.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：惠帝承太祖遺威余烈，國勢初張，仁聞昭宣，眾心悅附。

translations.literal: The eulogist says: Emperor Hui inherited the Founding Emperor's remaining might and blazing force; the state's power was just expanding; benevolence was heard and proclaimed; the people's hearts were pleased and attached.
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: Emperor Hui inherited the Hongwu Emperor's prestige when the dynasty was still rising in strength; his benevolence was proclaimed abroad, and the people were glad to follow him.

sentences.zh: 成祖奮起方隅，冒不韙以爭天下，未嘗有萬全之計也。

translations.literal: Chengzu roused himself in a corner, braved impropriety to contend for the realm, and never had a plan of complete security.
translations.idiomatic: The Yongle Emperor rose from a remote principality, defied convention to contest the throne, and never had a sure plan for victory.

sentences.zh: 乃道衍首贊密謀，發機決策。

translations.literal: Then Daoyan first approved secret counsel and released the trigger of decision.
translations.idiomatic: It was Daoyan who first urged the secret plot and shaped the decisive strategy.

sentences.zh: 張玉、朱能之輩戮力行間，轉戰無前，隕身不顧。

translations.literal: Zhang Yu, Zhu Neng, and their kind exerted themselves in the ranks, turned from battle without looking back, and gave their lives without regard.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yu, Zhu Neng, and their comrades fought with desperate courage at the front, swept from battle to battle, and gave their lives without hesitation.

sentences.zh: 於是收勁旅，摧雄師，四年而成帝業。

translations.literal: Thereby he gathered crack troops, shattered mighty armies, and in four years accomplished the imperial enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Thus he gathered elite troops, shattered powerful armies, and won the empire in four years.

sentences.zh: 意者天之所興，群策群力，應時並濟。

translations.literal: Perhaps it was what Heaven was raising; many counsels and many strengths responded to the time and aided together.
translations.idiomatic: Perhaps Heaven willed it; many minds and many hands answered the moment together.

sentences.zh: 諸人之得為功臣首也，可不謂厚幸哉！

translations.literal: That these men came to stand at the head of the merit ministers—can it not be called great good fortune!
translations.idiomatic: That these men came to rank among the foremost of the dynasty's merit lords—was this not extraordinary good fortune!
